items.title: Internals
items.text:
This page documents Consist's internal persistence schema, digest schemes, signature construction, location freshness verification, and migration pipeline. It is intended for Consist contributors and power users inspecting provenance.duckdb directly.

For the user-facing mental model, see How Consist Works.

items.title: Core Data Model
items.text: In user-facing code, an Artifact ties together three concepts: its name (art.key), its fingerprint (art.digest), and its location (art.path / art.uri). Inside provenance.duckdb, Consist records runs, artifacts, content identities, run-artifact bindings, and location witnesses via SQLModel + DuckDB (consist.core.persistence.DatabaseManager).

items.title: Mapping User-Facing Terms to Store Tables
items.text: User-facing concept Public v0.5 API Internal store representation Fingerprint art.digest (Digest(scheme, hex)) artifact_content(id, content_hash, driver, ...) and artifact.hash / artifact.content_id Name art.key, inputs/outputs keys run_artifact_link(run_id, artifact_id, direction) and artifact.key Location art.path, art.uri artifact.container_uri + artifact_location(artifact_id, uri, witness_json, ...) Artifact Artifact artifact(id, key, driver, container_uri, hash, content_id, run_id, parent_artifact_id, ...) Run Run run(id, model_name, status, stage, phase, git_hash, config_hash, input_hash, signature, ...)

items.title: Execution Modes (Tracker)
items.text:
Consist supports three execution modes depending on db_path and run_dir:

  1. Full Provenance Mode (db_path=<path>, run_dir=<path>): Dual-writes run and artifact records to provenance.duckdb and consist.json, computes content digests according to hashing_strategy, and enables full caching and SQL querying.
  2. JSON-Only Mode (db_path=None, run_dir=<path>): Computes full digests and writes consist.json snapshots inside run_dir without opening DuckDB. Useful for DB-less distributed workers whose provenance can later be reconstructed into a central DuckDB store via tracker.rebuild_from_json().
  3. Ephemeral Mode (db_path=None, run_dir=None): Creates no directories, opens no DuckDB database, writes no consist.json, and uses lightweight FileStat fingerprints with sub-millisecond overhead.

items.title: Signature Composition
items.text:
Consist computes a single unified content-addressed signature across tracker.run(), scenario.run(), and trace():

signature = SHA256(code_identity || config_identity || bound_inputs || declared_outputs)
  1. Code Identity (code_hash):
  2. repo_git (default): Git HEAD commit SHA plus dirty working-tree state.
  3. callable_module: SHA-256 of the Python module file defining the unwrapped callable, plus any declared extra_deps.
  4. callable_source: SHA-256 of the unwrapped callable's source code, plus any declared extra_deps.
  5. Container steps record the container image digest, command, environment digest, backend, working directory, and virtualized volume mounts.
  6. Config Identity (config_hash):
  7. Canonical JSON serialization with sorted keys, normalized numeric types, deterministic Pydantic model serialization, and adapter-provided config facets/identity inputs.
  8. Role-Aware Input Bindings (input_hash):
  9. Ordered by binding role/key. Each input binding contributes its parameter name, its verified digest, and any sub-artifact selector (such as an HDF5 table path or Zarr variable key).
  10. Resolved filesystem paths are never hashed into input_hash.
  11. Declared Output Specifications:
  12. When outputs are declared upfront via outputs={...} (e.g., outputs={"cleaned": "cleaned.parquet"}), the declared output names and filenames/extensions are included in config_hash without baking resolved host workspace directories (run_dir) into the signature.

items.title: Location Witnesses & Freshness Verification
items.text:
To avoid re-hashing gigabytes of unchanged data on every step while still catching out-of-band file modifications, consist.location provides typed location witnesses:

  • FileStat: Records (size, mtime_ns, inode) and digest_verified for a single file (with no persisted racy field).
  • DirTreeStat: Records directory-level and member-level stat summaries and digest_verified for directory trees and Zarr stores (with no persisted racy field).

Before executing a step with pre-existing declared output targets, Consist snapshots pre-step stats/digests and raises StaleOutputError if a pre-existing output file, directory/Zarr store, or HDF5 member was left untouched on disk.

For coordinate translation, candidate precedence, and witness verification invariants, see Location Resolver Architecture.

items.title: Dual-Write Order
items.text:
Every run in Full Provenance Mode maintains two persistence records:

  1. consist.json (Per-Run Snapshot): Written atomically inside run_dir for human-readable inspection and JSON-based recovery (rebuild_from_json()).
  2. provenance.duckdb (DatabaseManager): Commits the run, artifact, link, and location records inside an explicit DuckDB transaction.

items.title: consist migrate Pipeline
items.text:
consist migrate <db_path> upgrades a Consist 0.4.x database to 0.5 out-of-place:

  1. Out-of-place staging: Reads the 0.4.x database read-only and builds a verified 0.5 staging database.
  2. Verification & --trust-v04-hashes: Verifies surviving files on disk (or trusts existing v0.4 SHA-256 hashes when --trust-v04-hashes is passed), marking missing/unverified historical entries so they never produce unsafe cache hits.
  3. Atomic backup & swap: Saves the original database to <db_path>.v04.bak and swaps the verified staging database into place, supporting consist migrate undo <db_path> for reversibility.

items.title: Consist LLM Skill
items.text:
Consist includes an LLM-provider-agnostic skill for agents that help users instrument downstream scientific workflows. The skill packages project-specific guidance for bootstrapping Consist, wrapping legacy file-writing steps, debugging cache and provenance behavior, inspecting runs, and querying recorded artifacts.

The canonical skill lives in the repository at skills/consist/.

items.title: When to use it
items.text:
Use the skill when asking an agent to:

  • add Consist to a new project or pipeline;
  • choose between run(...), trace(...), exec(...) / consist exec, and scenario(...);
  • wrap external tools, containers, or legacy code that writes files;
  • declare outputs, output sets, schema profiles, and cache identity;
  • inspect or analyze recorded runs and artifacts;
  • debug cache misses, hydration, mount resolution, or scenario wiring.

items.title: Install
items.text:
Download or clone the Consist repository and copy the full skills/consist/ folder into your agent tool's skill directory. Preserve the folder layout; SKILL.md depends on the files under references/.

For Codex, the default install shape is:

git clone https://github.com/LBNL-UCB-STI/consist.git
mkdir -p "${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/skills"
cp -R consist/skills/consist "${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/skills/"

For active development from a local Consist checkout, use a symlink instead so skill edits stay in sync:

mkdir -p "${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/skills"
ln -s "$(pwd)/skills/consist" "${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/skills/consist"

items.title: Maintain
items.text:
Keep canonical guidance in skills/consist/SKILL.md and skills/consist/references/. Provider-specific files such as skills/consist/agents/openai.yaml are optional UI metadata.

After editing the skill, validate it with your agent platform's skill validator. With Codex's skill-creator tooling, the command shape is:

python path/to/skill-creator/scripts/quick_validate.py path/to/skills/consist

items.title: Location Resolver Architecture
items.text: This page documents the internal architecture of Consist's Layer-2 location resolution, coordinate translation, epoch synchronization, and stat-witness verification pipeline. It is intended for contributors working on location.py, fs.py, persistence.py, location_resolver.py, tracker_recovery.py, tracker_archive.py, cache.py, materialize.py, and workflow.py.

items.title: 1. Overview & Component Architecture
items.text:
Consist separates location coordinates and stat witnesses (value types), host path translation (containment-checked filesystem mapping), ledger persistence (DuckDB + epoch invalidation), and candidate precedence (unified lazy enumeration) into distinct layers:

flowchart TD
    LOC["src/consist/location.py<br/>FileStat · DirTreeStat · ArtifactLocationRow · TranslatedCoordinate"]
    FS["src/consist/core/fs.py<br/>FileSystemManager<br/>(containment-checked translation, root realpath caching)"]
    DB["src/consist/core/persistence.py<br/>DatabaseManager<br/>(artifact_location ledger, epochs, witness settlement)"]
    RES["src/consist/core/location_resolver.py<br/>LocationResolver<br/>(sync_epoch, prefetch, iter_candidates)"]

    REC["tracker_recovery.py<br/>verify_and_settle_candidate<br/>resolve_verified_local_path_detailed"]
    CACHE["cache.py<br/>hydration & validation"]
    MAT["materialize.py<br/>rematerialization & staging"]
    ARCH["tracker_archive.py<br/>archive source selection<br/>superseded recovery-root eviction"]
    WF["workflow.py<br/>coupler snapshot restore<br/>append_artifacts_recovery_roots_bulk"]

    LOC --> FS
    LOC --> DB
    FS --> RES
    DB --> RES
    RES --> REC
    RES --> CACHE
    RES --> MAT
    RES --> ARCH
    RES --> WF
    ARCH --> WF
  • LocationResolver (aliased as MountPrecedenceResolver) is bound lazily to each Tracker via tracker.location_resolver and serves as the single canonical source of candidate paths across recovery, cache validation, materialization, archiving, and coupler restoration.

items.title: 2. Coordinate Translation & Three-View Symlink Semantics
items.text:
Every coordinate translation via FileSystemManager.translate_location_coordinate (and translate_raw_root) produces a TranslatedCoordinate with status in {"resolved", "unmounted", "rejected"} and three distinct path views:

View Construction Symlink Semantics Primary Consumer lexical_path lexical_root / rel_parts All symlinks visible (mount root and in-mount components) Symlink rejection probes, invert_relative_layout mount_canonical_lexical_path canonical_root / rel_parts Mount root resolved (realpath); in-mount symlinks visible Symlink rejection probes inside a symlinked mount root (e.g. /var → /private/var) canonical_path Parent-canonicalized, leaf-preserving Ancestor resolved; leaf name preserved if leaf itself is a symlink Deduplication (seen_canonical), existence/digest checks

items.title: Single-Pass Containment
items.text:
FileSystemManager's containment check in src/consist/core/fs.py establishes containment without requiring the target file to exist yet:

  1. Starts at probe = Path(os.path.abspath(candidate)) and walks upward using os.lstat(probe) (not exists(), so dangling symlinks do not look like missing files and instead fall through to strict resolution).
  2. Collects any missing trailing path components in tail.
  3. Once an existing ancestor is found, calls probe.resolve(strict=True). Dangling symlinks, symlink loops (RuntimeError), or unreadable components (OSError) return None, which callers treat as a fail-closed rejection.
  4. If tail is non-empty, joins reversed(tail) lexically onto base and returns (joined, joined).
  5. If tail is empty and the leaf itself is a symlink (stat.S_ISLNK), returns (base, Path(os.path.realpath(probe.parent)) / probe.name) so containment is checked against the resolved target base while canonical_path preserves the leaf name.

For mounted/rooted coordinates, FileSystemManager first rejects any .. segment in the relative path before joining, then verifies target.is_relative_to(canonical_root) and returns rejected_coordinate(...) if the resolved path escapes the root.

items.title: Fail-Closed mount_name == "abs" Containment
items.text:
When mount_name == "abs", translate_location_coordinate:

  1. Strips a leading file:// prefix (returning unmounted_coordinate if empty).
  2. Rejects any .. segment in PurePosixPath(stripped).parts immediately.
  3. Performs single-pass containment resolution on Path(stripped) and returns rejected_coordinate(...) if containment fails (dangling symlink, loop, or unreadable component).

items.title: Root Realpath Caching
items.text: FileSystemManager caches resolved root metadata (lexical_root, canonical_root, inst_id) keyed by (self.run_dir, self.sorted_mounts_key). Changing run_dir or mounts automatically invalidates the cache on the next lookup.

items.title: 3. Canonical Candidate Precedence & Lazy Tiering
items.text:
LocationResolver.iter_candidates(...) yields deduplicated (by canonical_path), containment-checked ResolvedCandidate instances in strict precedence order:

Tier ResolvedCandidate.source Origin Notes 1 "explicit_root" source_root argument Combined with remappable_relative_path(artifact) via translate_raw_root 2 "runtime_abs" artifact.abs_path Emitted only when include_runtime_abs=True 4a "ledger_primary" resolve_primary_coordinate(row, artifact) Evaluated across all active ArtifactLocationRows first 4b "ledger_historical" iter_historical_coordinates(row, artifact) Lazy fallback across active rows (excluding Tier 4a canonical_paths) 5a "historical_uri" artifact.meta["mount_root"] Combined with unprefixed_uri_relative_path(artifact.uri) 5b "historical_uri" Owning Run / historical_run / historical_run_dir Resolved via fs.get_historical_root(...) 5c "managed_mount" Current-run managed mount Emitted when (not candidate_rows and is_current_run) or include_current_uri

Within Tier 4b (iter_historical_coordinates), historical roots for non-abs named mounts are gathered in order from: (1) owning-run metadata (mounts / archive_mounts), (2) artifact.meta["mount_root"], and (3) DB historical mount index (get_live_historical_mount_roots then get_historical_mount_roots). Candidates are ranked (0: target exists, 1: root/prefix exists, 2: remaining non-rejected) while skipping os.path.exists probes on roots already known to be dead in the current epoch.

items.title: Why Tier 4a Precedes Tier 4b
items.text: iter_candidates exhausts resolve_primary_coordinate across every active row (Tier 4a) before entering iter_historical_coordinates (Tier 4b). On HPC clusters, historical rows often point to unmounted or slow Lustre/NFS $SCRATCH filesystems; resolving and verifying an active local workspace or archive coordinate in Tier 4a short-circuits iteration before any historical root is probed.

items.title: Bulk Prefetch & Rejection Callbacks
items.text:
• LocationResolver.prefetch(artifacts, runs=()) calls sync_epoch(), bulk-loads active location rows via db.get_active_artifact_locations_bulk into its per-epoch location-row cache, and bulk-loads owning runs via db.get_runs_by_ids_chronological into its per-epoch run cache.
  • Callers can pass on_rejected: Callable[[TranslatedCoordinate], None] to iter_candidates to inspect rejected coordinates (for example, to record symlink rejections) without altering candidate enumeration.

items.title: 4. Epoch Synchronization
items.text:
DatabaseManager maintains two independent process-local epoch maps in src/consist/core/persistence.py, keyed by the resolved database path:

  • Location epoch (via effective_location_epoch, sync_location_epoch_caches, bump_location_epoch): incremented on artifact_location writes, witness updates, and evictions. Invalidates location resolution caches, ephemeral stale location state, settled-witness caches, active coordinate witnesses, and registered epoch invalidation hooks.
  • Mount epoch (via effective_mount_epoch, sync_mount_epoch_caches, bump_mount_epoch): incremented only when mount history changes. Invalidates historical mount caches.

Keeping these two epochs separate ensures that ordinary artifact_location writes do not thrash historical mount caches. For read-only connections, both effective_location_epoch and effective_mount_epoch also include the DB and WAL file stat stamps ((mtime, size)) so sibling Tracker handles pointing at the same DuckDB file immediately observe writes and new mounts from other handles or processes. LocationResolver.sync_epoch() tracks the location epoch ((db.effective_location_epoch, fs.workspace_instance_id)) and mount epoch ((db.effective_mount_epoch, fs.sorted_mounts_key)) separately, clearing its location-row and run caches on location-epoch changes and its historical-mount caches on mount-epoch changes.

items.title: 5. Persisted digest_verified Witnesses
items.text:
FileStat and DirTreeStat in src/consist/location.py carry digest_verified: bool = False, serialized inside the witness_json JSON column of artifact_location. Storing digest_verified inside the witness JSON avoids requiring a DuckDB schema migration while keeping verification state co-located with the stat tuple (without persisted racy state, avoiding 2x Lustre reads and read-time DB writes on first-consumer jobs).

verify_and_settle_candidate in src/consist/core/tracker_recovery.py enforces three invariants:

  1. Unverified FRESH witnesses cannot bless tampered bytes: when WitnessFreshness.FRESH is returned, it fast-paths (return True, False) only if not verify_digest and either the artifact has no portable content identity or effective_witness.digest_verified is True. Otherwise it runs verify_candidate_against_artifact(path, artifact) and settles with with_digest_verified(True).
  2. Race-safe stat-mismatch & witnessless verification: when WitnessFreshness.STAT_MISMATCH (with portable content identity) or effective_witness is None is encountered, verify_and_settle_candidate captures pre_w, verifies the content digest, captures post_w, and calls db.settle_artifact_location_witness(...) only if pre_w == post_w.
  3. Carry-forward & no-op UPDATE suppression:
  4. During artifact_location upserts in DatabaseManager, if an incoming row has loc.witness.digest_verified == False while the existing row has prev.witness.digest_verified == True, prev.digest == loc.digest, and prev.witness.with_digest_verified(False) == loc.witness.with_digest_verified(False), the existing digest_verified=True flag is carried forward onto loc.
  5. DatabaseManager.settle_artifact_location_witness checks both its in-memory settled-witness cache and the persisted witness_json row; if existing_witness == verified_witness, it returns without issuing a DuckDB UPDATE, avoiding unnecessary write transactions across fresh SLURM jobs.

items.title: 6. Non-Obvious Invariants & Design Decisions
items.text:
• Excluding workspace / runs from archive recovery roots: in tracker_archive.py, source-mount recovery-root extraction returns None for workspace:// and runs:// URIs (and when the resolved mount root equals self.fs.run_dir) so workspace-local outputs are not redundantly registered as site="archive" recovery roots.
  • Multi-coordinate archive eviction: when an archive root is overwritten, tracker_archive.py constructs eviction coordinates for the normalized archive coordinate, ("abs", "", f"file://{resolved_target}"), ("abs", "", f"file://{lexical_target}"), and any active or historical named-mount alias where resolved_target.is_relative_to(resolved_mount), then passes them together to db.evict_recovery_root_locations(...). For schemes with multiple historical mount roots where only a subset match the target, eviction filters rows in SQL by relative archive subpath and checks each row's owning run mount (falling back to coordinate resolution only when no owning mount is recorded) so rows pointing outside the overwritten root stay active.
  • Lazy per-candidate symlink rejection: LocationResolver.iter_candidates yields candidates lazily, and archive source selection in tracker_archive.py checks for symlink components on cand.lexical_path and cand.mount_canonical_lexical_path per candidate, recording the first rejected symlink path and continuing rather than aborting. An unrelated historical symlink therefore never poisons a clean primary candidate.
  • unprefixed_rel climb guard & parent-to-child recovery: FileSystemManager.invert_relative_layout(target_path, rel_path) requires len(target_parts) > len(rel_parts) (strictly greater, preventing climbing above filesystem root). In resolve_verified_local_path_detailed, when a child artifact with parent_artifact_id (such as an OutputSet member) has no direct hit, recovery resolves parent via LocationResolver.iter_candidates, inverts parent_rel with invert_relative_layout, and translates rel_path under parent_root via fs.translate_raw_root.
  • Coupler snapshot bulk recovery registration: during coupler snapshot restoration in src/consist/core/workflow.py, restored artifacts with resolved source roots are collected into pending_recovery_roots and committed in one batch via self.tracker._archive_service.append_artifacts_recovery_roots_bulk(pending_recovery_roots) (single DB transaction and sidecar pass).

items.title: Upgrading to Consist 0.5
items.text: Consist 0.5.0 introduces a cleaner provenance database layout that separates what a file contains (its fingerprint), how a step used it (its role), and where valid copies currently live on disk (its known locations). Existing 0.4.x workflows continue to run with minimal or zero code changes after a one-command database upgrade.

items.title: 1. Upgrading Your Provenance Database (consist migrate)
items.text: When Consist 0.5 opens a 0.4.x DuckDB file directly, it stops and raises DatabaseMigrationRequired rather than modifying your file silently.

items.title: Standard One-Command Upgrade
items.text:
Run consist migrate on your provenance.duckdb file:

consist migrate provenance.duckdb

What consist migrate does:

  1. Out-of-place build: Reads your 0.4.x database read-only and builds a verified 0.5 database in a temporary staging file.
  2. Automatic backup: Keeps your original 0.4.x file untouched as provenance.duckdb.v04.bak in the same directory before swapping the upgraded database into place.
  3. Verification gates: Verifies run counts, artifact counts, ingested tables, and file fingerprints before completing the cutover.

You can preview what the upgrade will do without writing any files using --dry-run:

consist migrate provenance.duckdb --dry-run

items.title: Trusting v0.4 Hashes for Large Archives (--trust-v04-hashes)
items.text:
If your 0.4.x database already contains verified SHA-256 hashes for large cold archives on disk and you want to migrate without re-reading every file from disk, pass --trust-v04-hashes:

consist migrate provenance.duckdb --trust-v04-hashes

When --trust-v04-hashes is passed, consist migrate trusts existing v0.4 SHA-256 hashes without re-hashing files on disk. Unverified or missing files remain visible in lineage and queries as historical fingerprints.

items.title: Reversibility (consist migrate undo)
items.text:
If you need to switch back to your 0.4.x database backup at any point:

consist migrate undo provenance.duckdb

items.title: 2. How Historical Runs Behave After Migration
items.text:
When a historical file from 0.4.x was already deleted from scratch storage before the upgrade (or only had a quick size-and-timestamp check):

  • Already-verified artifacts work immediately: Any artifact that already had a full SHA-256 file fingerprint, a directory manifest, a logical matrix fingerprint, or an ingested DuckDB table in 0.4.x is ready for cache hits and queries right away.
  • Unverified historical artifacts stay queryable but never cause false cache hits: In 0.4.x, fast hashing recorded file size and modification time rather than full content bytes. After migration, unverified historical entries remain visible in run history and lineage queries, but Consist marks their fingerprints as historical-only so they never produce an unsafe cache hit.

items.title: 3. What's New in the 0.5 Python API (and What Stays Compatible)
Symmetric inputs={...} and outputs={...} with : Path Annotations
items.text:
In 0.5, you can declare both inputs and outputs as name -> path dictionaries and annotate your function parameters with : Path. Consist injects local Path objects for both inputs and outputs and verifies that declared outputs exist when the function returns:

from pathlib import Path
import pandas as pd
from consist import Tracker

tracker = Tracker(run_dir="./runs", db_path="./provenance.duckdb")


def clean_data(raw: Path, cleaned: Path, threshold: float = 0.5) -> None:
    df = pd.read_parquet(raw)
    df[df["value"] > threshold].to_parquet(cleaned, index=False)


result = tracker.run(
    fn=clean_data,
    inputs={"raw": "raw.parquet"},
    outputs={"cleaned": "cleaned.parquet"},
    config={"threshold": 0.5},
)

[!NOTE] Full Backward Compatibility: Existing functions that return dict[str, Path] with outputs=["cleaned"] and ExecutionOptions(input_binding="paths") continue to work without modification.

items.title: Direct .path and .as_df() on Every Artifact
items.text:
Every Artifact handle returned in result.outputs[...] is now an immutable, picklable object with two primary conveniences:

  • art.path: Resolves a live local Path to a valid copy of the file (automatically falling back to archived copies if a scratch file was moved or evicted).
  • art.as_df(): Loads tabular data (Parquet, CSV, HDF5 table, or ingested DuckDB table) directly into a pandas.DataFrame.
cleaned = result.outputs["cleaned"]
print(cleaned.path)
df = cleaned.as_df()

items.title: Smarter Coupler Path Auto-Detection
items.text:
Coupler now accepts Path or str values directly in coupler.set("skims", path) (lazily observing the file into an Artifact when read) and resolves paths via coupler.path("skims"):

skims_path = coupler.path("skims")

items.title: Removal of NoopTracker and enabled=False
items.text:
NoopTracker, NoopScenarioContext, NoopCoupler, LocalRef, NoopArtifact, and noop_scenario have been removed in 0.5.0. Passing enabled=False to consist.scenario(...), consist.create_tracker(...), or top-level logging helpers now raises ValueError immediately (enabled=True continues to work for backward compatibility, and consist.create_tracker(...) is deprecated in favor of instantiating Tracker(...) directly).

For lightweight runs without a DuckDB database, instantiate a DB-less Tracker:

from consist import Tracker

tracker = Tracker(run_dir="./runs", db_path=None)

items.title: Analytical Queries Without SQLAlchemy Sessions (query_df, query_rows, config_run_rows)
items.text:
Consist 0.5.0 removes duckdb-engine, consist.db_session(), and SQLAlchemy Executable-based consist.run_query(...), routing all provenance and analytical SQL through a single native DuckDB connection:

  • Replace raw SQL or DataFrame queries with tracker.query_df(sql, params=...) (or consist.query_df(...)).
  • Replace ORM model queries with tracker.query_rows(sql, params=..., model=MyModel) (or consist.query_rows(..., model=MyModel)), which validates rows into Pydantic or SQLModel instances.
  • Replace config-table SQLAlchemy joins with consist.config_run_rows(MyConfigModel, link_table=MyConfigRunLink, where={"key": "sample_rate"}, tracker=tracker) or consist.pivot_facets(...) (which now returns a ParameterizedSQL(sql, params) pair ready for tracker.query_df(q.sql, q.params)).
  • Legacy dynamic ORM view helpers (consist.view(...), consist.register_views(...), tracker.view(...), tracker.register_views(...)) now raise DeprecatedViewsError with migration guidance; create SQL hybrid views via tracker.create_view("v_persons", "persons") and query them with tracker.query_df(...), tracker.query_rows(..., model=Person), or consist.ibis_view(tracker, model=Person).
from consist import ParameterizedSQL, pivot_facets

df = tracker.query_df(
    "SELECT id, model_name FROM run WHERE status = ?",
    ["completed"],
)

q: ParameterizedSQL = pivot_facets(keys=["sample_rate", "seed"], namespace="sim")
facet_df = tracker.query_df(q.sql, q.params)

items.title: Ephemeral Mode (Tracker()) and JSON-Only Mode (db_path=None, run_dir=...)
items.text:
• Ephemeral Mode (Tracker() with db_path=None, run_dir=None) replaces NoopTracker: it creates no directories, writes no database or consist.json, and uses lightweight file-stat fingerprints with sub-millisecond overhead.
  • JSON-Only Mode (Tracker(run_dir=..., db_path=None)) writes full SHA-256 digests and consist.json snapshots without opening DuckDB, so distributed workers can later be reconstructed into a central database via tracker.rebuild_from_json().

items.title: Practical 0.5 Ergonomics & Gotchas
items.text:
• Deep-frozen Artifact.meta (MappingProxyType / FrozenList): Artifact.meta deep-freezes nested dicts into MappingProxyType and lists into FrozenList, so a shallow dict(artifact.meta) leaves nested dicts as MappingProxyType (causing json.dumps(dict(artifact.meta)) to fail with TypeError) and isinstance(meta.get("facet"), dict) evaluates to False. Check isinstance(..., collections.abc.Mapping) for read-only inspection, or call artifact.meta_dict() (or artifact.to_json_dict()["meta"] / consist.digest.normalize_json(artifact.meta)) when you need plain dict/list containers for JSON serialization.
  • shutil.copy2 under unified outputs={role: path}: Because unified outputs={role: path} snapshots pre-existing target files and raises StaleOutputError if bytes + mtime are unchanged after the step runs, using shutil.copy2 onto an already-existing target path (preserving the old mtime alongside identical bytes) will trip StaleOutputError. Use fresh step-owned paths or update target mtime intentionally when overwriting identical bytes.
  • In-process DuckDB read_only=True conflicts: DuckDB raises a configuration error if a read-write Tracker and a separate duckdb.connect(db_path, read_only=True) connection open the same file in the same process. Use Tracker(..., access_mode="read_only") (which coordinates live connections via lookup_live_db_by_path), or close the writer first with tracker.close() / with Tracker(...) as tracker:.
  • archive_run_outputs with external outputs: Artifacts written outside Tracker.run_dir must be backed by configured mounts={...} on the Tracker so archive_run_outputs(...) can resolve their mounted URIs and recreate relative paths under archive_root. Avoid mounting a parent directory of run_dir or reusing the reserved "workspace" scheme name (since mounts are checked before run_dir and workspace:// has special ephemeral fallback semantics); mount sibling output directories directly instead.
  • Primary workspace existence check vs. recovery fallback: artifact.path / artifact.as_path(tracker) transparently fall back to registered archive recovery roots when primary files under run_dir have been pruned. Callers checking whether primary workspace files are materialized before calling hydrate_run_outputs(...) should check Path(tracker.resolve_uri(artifact.uri)).exists() or tracker.resolve_artifact_path(artifact, allow_recovery_roots=False).
  • DatabaseMaintenance.merge() vs. bare global_tables.* DDL: DatabaseMaintenance.merge() automatically clones dlt-managed global_tables.* schemas (including _dlt_load_id and _dlt_id) into an empty destination database. Do not pre-create bare SQL global_tables.* tables without those columns on a fresh destination database before merging dlt-ingested shards.

items.title: 4. Multi-Environment Safety
items.text:
If you work across multiple Python or Conda environments on the same machine or HPC cluster:

  • Consist 0.4.2+ checks the database schema version on startup and raises a clear IncompatibleSchemaError with upgrade instructions if you accidentally point an older environment at a migrated 0.5 database.
  • Consist 0.4.1 and earlier will fail fast with a DuckDB Binder Error (or Cannot insert into view "artifact_content") because 0.5 installs read-only compatibility views that block legacy writes from corrupting 0.5 provenance records. See Troubleshooting if you encounter either message.

items.title: Mounts & Portability
items.text:
Consist stores portable URIs where it can, instead of baking in one machine's absolute paths. Mounts let each machine map the same logical URI scheme to its own filesystem.

Recommended path

Use tracker.run(...), tracker.trace(...), or scenario.run(...) for normal workflows. This page focuses on path behavior and URI mechanics.

items.title: Mounts at a Glance
items.text:
Mounts map a short scheme to a local root:

from consist import Tracker

tracker = Tracker(
    run_dir="./runs",
    db_path="./provenance.duckdb",
    mounts={
        "inputs": "/shared/inputs",
        "outputs": "/scratch/outputs",
    },
)

Artifacts under those roots are stored as URIs:

inputs://land_use.csv
outputs://baseline/results.parquet

Another user can open the same provenance database with different physical paths, as long as the mount names keep the same meaning.

items.title: What Mounts Do Not Do
items.text:
Mounts make paths portable; they do not replicate bytes.

Situation Result Current machine can resolve the URI and the file exists Artifact bytes are usable Current machine can resolve the URI but the file is missing Metadata remains, byte access fails or skips Current machine lacks the mount Consist cannot safely resolve the URI Artifact has recovery_roots Hydration may find archived bytes elsewhere

For durable archived outputs, see Historical Recovery.

items.title: Container Volumes
items.text:
For container runs, keep in-container paths stable and map host roots through tracker mounts:

from pathlib import Path

from consist.integrations.containers import run_container

inputs_root = Path(tracker.mounts["inputs"]).resolve()
runs_root = Path(tracker.run_dir).resolve()

container = run_container(
    tracker=tracker,
    run_id="model_step",
    image="my-model:1.0",
    command=["python", "/app/run.py", "--input", "/inputs/data.csv"],
    volumes={
        str(inputs_root): "/inputs",
        str(runs_root): "/outputs",
    },
    inputs=[inputs_root / "data.csv"],
    outputs=[runs_root / "model" / "summary.csv"],
    backend_type="docker",
)

Guidelines:

  • Use stable container paths such as /inputs and /outputs.
  • Use tracker mounts for machine-specific host paths.
  • Keep strict_mounts=True unless an external path is intentional.
  • Remember that the container run signature currently includes resolved host volume paths, so different host roots can miss cache even if mounted data is logically the same.

See Container Guide for runnable container examples.

items.title: Run-Local Outputs
items.text:
Paths under the run directory are usually stored relative to the active run:

./outputs/<run_id>/model.csv

Historical resolution uses the producing run's _physical_run_dir metadata for workspace-relative paths. If that directory moves or is deleted, metadata-only cache hits can still work, but byte access needs a recovery path.

items.title: Historical Path Resolution
items.text:
When Consist needs bytes from a prior run, it resolves paths in this order:

  1. Per-call source_root=... override.
  2. Workspace-relative paths under the producing run's _physical_run_dir.
  3. Mount-backed URIs through the historical mount snapshot or current mounts.
  4. Ordered artifact.meta["recovery_roots"].
  5. DuckDB export fallback for ingested tabular artifacts.

Absolute paths and file://... URIs are treated conservatively. Consist avoids silently reinterpreting them under unrelated roots.

items.title: Sharing A Database
items.text:
Sharing a DuckDB provenance file across machines is supported when the team agrees on mount names and each user maps those names locally.

Recommended practice:

  • Use shared mount names such as inputs, outputs, scratch, and archive.
  • Keep the database in a shared location with write access controls.
  • Archive or ingest outputs that must survive workspace cleanup.
  • Record recovery_roots when archived bytes should remain discoverable.

items.title: Cache-Hit File Behavior
items.text:
Function runs and container runs differ:

Surface Default cache-hit bytes behavior tracker.run(...) / scenario.run(...) Hydrate metadata only unless output materialization is requested run_container(...) Materialize cached outputs to requested host output paths hydrate_run_outputs(...) Restore selected historical outputs into a target root

Use cache_hydration="outputs-requested" when a function step needs selected output files copied on cache hit. Use historical recovery APIs for restart or workspace rebuild flows.

items.title: Best Practices
items.text:
• Prefer mount-backed paths for shared data and archived outputs.
  • Treat run directories as local workspaces, not durable archives.
  • Keep artifact identity canonical even when bytes are copied elsewhere.
  • Record recovery_roots once instead of passing ad hoc source roots forever.
  • Prefer hydrate_run_outputs(...) over legacy aggregate materialization for new restart or recovery code.
  • Keep external target paths opt-in with allow_external_paths=True.

items.title: Troubleshooting
items.text:
• Cache hit but file missing: Check the original run directory, mount map, and recovery_roots.
  • URI does not resolve: Add the missing mount or use a tracker configured with the same mount names used by the producer.
  • Moved run directory: Metadata can still hydrate, but workspace-relative bytes need an archive, recovery root, or DB fallback.
  • Container cache miss across machines: Compare resolved host volume roots; those paths are part of the container signature today.

items.title: See Also
items.text:
• Container Guide
  • Caching & Hydration
  • Historical Recovery
  • Materialization API

items.title: Consist provenance schema
items.text:
Consist publishes two small, experimental LinkML modules for portable provenance handoffs. They are a durable provenance graph and optional cache-aware invocation contract—not an ORM export, registry, complete execution-observation model, or LinkML runtime dependency.

  • src/consist/schemas/provenance.yaml supplies ledger context, runs, artifacts, trusted identities, parent structure, and input/output lineage edges.
  • src/consist/schemas/binding.yaml imports the provenance graph and adds optional cache-aware binding invocation facts.

Both modules are schema version 0.1.0, independently versioned from the Consist Python package. A package release can ship the same unchanged schema version; an additive optional field is normally compatible, while removing or renaming a class or slot, changing a required field, or changing identity meaning is a deliberate breaking schema change.

items.title: Durable provenance graph
items.text:
ConsistProvenanceDocument is a portable handoff envelope. It carries a required ConsistProvenanceContext and optional lists of runs, artifacts, and associations. The context has a stable namespace and an optional locator. The logical identity of a run or artifact is (namespace, local ID). The locator is mutable retrieval metadata and is never identity-bearing: it must not affect equality, deduplication, namespace assignment, or the identity used to compare references.

Every run or artifact may carry its own optional provenance_context. When it is omitted inside a ConsistProvenanceDocument, the record inherits the enclosing document context. A record-level context overrides the enclosing one. A standalone reference with neither context is deliberately local to its containing handoff and cannot safely be merged with a different document. This lets identical local IDs remain distinct in separate Consist ledgers.

ConsistRunReference has a required public run_id and optional signature, model name, parent run, and structured config/input/git identity evidence. ConsistArtifactReference has a required public UUID artifact_id and optional artifact key, Artifact.hash fingerprint, fingerprint strategy, trusted immutable identity, parent artifact, and producing run.

fingerprint is the broader portable Artifact.hash, whose hashing strategy can be content- or metadata-based. Artifact.content_id is a database-local deduplication key and never appears in these modules. immutable_identity is stronger and narrower: Consist currently attests only lowercase SHA-256 values with kind: file or kind: manifest-v1; do not infer one from a broader fingerprint alone.

ConsistRunArtifactAssociation records an input or output edge and always requires its run, artifact, and direction. role, binding_parameter, and is_implicit are optional evidence. A role is specific to an invocation and is not an alias for artifact_key.

An input edge says the run consumed or used the artifact and does not imply production. An output association says the run produced the artifact. If its artifact also supplies producing_run, that reference must resolve to the same run after context inheritance. An output association without producing_run is still a production assertion; consumers must not add a contradictory producer. Matching forms are two convenient views of one production fact, not two events. parent_artifact only preserves container/member structure; it is not an artifact derivation edge.

items.title: Optional cache-aware binding invocations
items.text:
Import binding.yaml only when a consumer needs to distinguish the current request from a prior cached result. ConsistBindingInvocationReference contains the required requested run, effective execution run, and cache outcome; the cache-source run and strict binding identity digest are optional.

Cache outcome requested run effective execution run cache-source run miss newly executing run same newly executing run omitted hit current invocation's new run historical producer same historical producer

For a cache miss, requested and effective execution runs must resolve to the same run and cache-source run must be absent. For a cache hit, effective execution and cache-source runs must resolve to the same historical producer; that producer must not be rewritten with the current request's input intent. The optional binding identity digest is a lowercase SHA-256 digest of a strict resolved-binding contract, not an artifact identity or the opaque binding JSON.

items.title: Scope boundary
items.text: The modules deliberately exclude mutable artifact locations and recovery paths; run status, timestamps, descriptions, tags, arbitrary metadata, and scenario fields; schema profiles and observations; complete manifests; admission reports and registry aliases; full resolved-binding JSON; and PILATES-owned scenario semantics. Domain roles such as a population snapshot or ATLAS vehicle output remain downstream-owned semantics.

items.title: Downstream composition
items.text:
Downstreams should pin and checksum an immutable merged release asset. Import the durable graph whenever an operational profile needs Consist lineage:

imports:
  - linkml:types
  - ./vendor/consist-provenance-0.1.1/provenance.merged

classes:
  PilatesAtlasVehicleArtifact:
    attributes:
      physical_artifact:
        range: ConsistArtifactReference
        required: true

Only a cache-aware adapter also imports ./vendor/consist-provenance-0.1.1/binding.merged.yaml (as binding.merged). The model-owned row schema remains independent of Consist. The local composition example is tests/fixtures/linkml/downstream_operational_profile.yaml.

consist:provenance and consist:binding are logical identifiers, not remote import resolvers in this release. Consumers must use a checked local asset rather than a mutable branch URL or network fetch during normal work.

items.title: Release assets and offline builds
items.text:
Each schema release publishes:

  • provenance.yaml and binding.yaml, the modular sources;
  • provenance.merged.yaml and binding.merged.yaml, their resolved import closures;
  • generated LinkML reference documentation under reference/provenance/ and reference/binding/;
  • SHA256SUMS, covering every shipped asset.

Create a new or empty release directory with the development-only LinkML toolchain:

uv run --group dev python scripts/build_provenance_schema_release.py \
  --output dist/provenance-schema-0.1.1

The corrected generated bundle is a prospective release-asset version 0.1.1; the unchanged provenance and binding vocabulary remains schema version 0.1.0. Do not replace the already checksummed 0.1.0 assets in place.

Merged assets record source_file_date and generation_date as timezone-aware UTC timestamps in Z notation. Before publishing, lint the modular sources and both merged assets, then verify the manifest:

linkml-lint dist/provenance-schema-0.1.1/provenance.yaml
linkml-lint dist/provenance-schema-0.1.1/binding.yaml
linkml-lint --ignore-warnings dist/provenance-schema-0.1.1/provenance.merged.yaml
linkml-lint --ignore-warnings dist/provenance-schema-0.1.1/binding.merged.yaml
(cd dist/provenance-schema-0.1.1 && sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS)

The merged lints ignore LinkML's standard_naming warnings for generator-created flattened slots such as ConsistRunReference__run_id; errors still fail the command. The builder rejects a nonempty output directory so stale generated pages cannot survive a schema rename or removal. A downstream build verifies SHA256SUMS before importing a merged asset. Python consumers may locate the packaged source with importlib.resources.files("consist.schemas"); normal import consist, tracking, caching, querying, recovery, persistence, and database migrations load neither linkml nor linkml_runtime.

The public LinkML Schema Registry is a later discovery mechanism, not a package manager, import resolver, or artifact-custody service. Register only after a downstream has successfully imported a released asset.

items.title: Schema Export (SQLModel Stubs)
items.text: Consist can capture the observed schema of tabular artifacts and export that schema as a static SQLModel class stub you can commit and edit. The export removes the mechanical work of retyping columns while keeping semantic choices in your hands.

items.title: What You Get
items.text:
• A Python 3.11 file containing one SQLModel class stub (exported as table=True).
  • Columns with:
  • a best-effort type mapping from DuckDB logical types
  • nullability (Optional[...] = None only when nullable)
  • deterministic ordering (prefers ordinal_position)
  • “Hints” as comments (enums/stats) when available (on by default).
  • Messy column names are handled: the generated attribute name is sanitized, but the original DB column name is preserved via Field(sa_column=Column("original", ...)) when needed.
  • Foreign keys are preserved if they were provided in a curated SQLModel schema (rendered as Field(foreign_key="table.column")).

items.title: Typical Workflow
items.text:
1. Ingest tabular data into DuckDB via log_dataframe(..., schema=MySchema) or enable lightweight file profiling with profile_file_schema=True. Consist captures the table structure automatically.
  2. Export the captured schema as a SQLModel stub (consist.cli schema export ...) and edit it to add primary keys, relationships, and normalization decisions.
  3. Register the curated model with a Tracker to activate a hybrid view for cross-run queries.

items.title: Abstract vs Concrete Exports
items.text:
By default, Consist exports SQLModel classes as abstract (__abstract__ = True). This keeps the stub importable immediately, because SQLAlchemy requires a primary key to map a concrete table/view, and many analysis tables don’t have an obvious primary key.

  • Default (recommended): abstract export, safe to import, great for view schemas.
  • Concrete export (advanced): export with --concrete (or abstract=False in Python) and then add a primary key before importing, otherwise SQLAlchemy will raise an error like “could not assemble any primary key columns”.

items.title: What You Still Do Manually
items.text:
Consist does not infer semantic intent. Treat the generated file as a starting point and edit it to add:

  • primary keys / foreign keys
  • indexes / uniqueness constraints
  • relationships
  • renames / normalization decisions

If you pass a curated SQLModel schema to log_artifact(..., schema=YourModel), Consist tags the artifact with that logical schema. If the model includes foreign_key=..., those FKs are persisted as schema metadata and will be re-emitted during export. This tagging is non-strict; validation only happens in separate ingestion or validation workflows.

items.title: Prerequisites
items.text:
Schema export uses the schema captured from a DuckDB-ingested table. In practice:

  1. You run with a database configured (db_path=...).
  2. You ingest tabular data into DuckDB (hot data).
  3. Consist profiles the ingested table and stores a deduped schema referenced by artifact.meta["schema_id"].

If you already see schema_id in an artifact’s meta, you’re ready to export.

You can also capture schemas without ingestion for CSV/Parquet artifacts by enabling lightweight file profiling at log time (profile_file_schema=True, optional file_schema_sample_rows=). This writes the same schema_id pointer into artifact.meta, allowing schema export even if the original file is later missing or moved.

For wrapped file-writing steps, enable profiling at the run level (Tracker.run(...) or ScenarioContext.run(...)) or at the individual output declaration:

from consist import ArtifactSpec

result = tracker.run(
    fn=run_step,
    inputs={"raw_firms": raw_firms_csv},
    output_paths={
        "synthetic_firms": ArtifactSpec(
            path=output_dir / "synthetic_firms.csv",
            schema=SyntheticFirms,
            profile_file_schema=True,
        )
    },
    profile_file_schema=True,
)

The run-level flag profiles tabular artifacts logged through the normal run lifecycle, including named Tracker.run(inputs={...}) or ScenarioContext.run(inputs={...}) inputs and declared output_paths. A per-output ArtifactSpec(profile_file_schema=...) overrides the run default for that output. schema=... on an ArtifactSpec is also a non-strict logical tag; it does not validate the file contents. These declarations apply when the artifact is logged. If a step returns from cache, newly added ArtifactSpec schema/profile metadata is not backfilled onto the cached artifact; use cache_mode="overwrite" or change the cache version/epoch when you need to persist new metadata for an already-cached output.

If an artifact was already logged without schema profiling, you can backfill file schema metadata later (as long as the file is still accessible):

python -m consist.cli schema capture-file --artifact-key trip_table

Use --artifact-id for UUID-based selection, and --path to override path resolution when the stored URI no longer resolves directly.

items.title: Exporting from the CLI
items.text:
Export by artifact UUID (recommended UX for now):

python -m consist.cli schema export \
  --artifact-id 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000 \
  --out your_pkg/models/persons.py

Or export by schema id (hash):

python -m consist.cli schema export \
  --schema-id <schema-hash> \
  --out your_pkg/models/persons.py

Useful flags:

  • --class-name Persons to override the generated class name
  • --table-name persons to override __tablename__
  • --include-system-cols to include system/ingestion columns like consist_* and _dlt_*
  • --no-stats-comments to omit stats/enum hint comments
  • --concrete to export a non-abstract mapped class (you must add a primary key)

If --out is omitted, the stub is printed to stdout (so it can be piped or redirected).

items.title: Exporting from Python
items.text:
You can generate the code (and optionally write it) from a Tracker:

from pathlib import Path
from consist import Tracker

tracker = Tracker(run_dir=".", db_path="provenance.duckdb")

code = tracker.export_schema_sqlmodel(
    artifact_id="00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000",
    out_path=Path("your_pkg/models/persons.py"),
    abstract=True,
)

The method returns the generated string regardless of whether you write it.

items.title: Best‑Effort Foreign Key Enforcement
items.text:
If you want DuckDB to attempt to enforce persisted foreign keys, run:

python -m consist.cli schema apply-fks

This step is best‑effort: if a constraint can’t be added (e.g., due to missing parent rows), Consist logs a warning and continues.

items.title: Where to Put the Generated File
items.text:
Place it anywhere importable by your project (on PYTHONPATH), for example:

  • your_pkg/models/
  • your_pkg/schemas/

If it’s a package directory, include an __init__.py so you can import your_pkg.models.persons.

Consist does not require a special directory layout; it only needs you to import the class and register it for views.

items.title: Using the Generated Model with Views
items.text:
Consist’s hybrid views are created from your SQLModel schema. To activate a view:

1) Import the model class. 2) Register it with the Tracker (at init time or after).

items.title: Register at Tracker initialization
items.text:
from consist import Tracker
from your_pkg.models.persons import Persons

tracker = Tracker(run_dir="./runs", db_path="./provenance.duckdb", schemas=[Persons])
tracker.create_view("v_persons", "persons")

items.title: Querying
items.text:
import consist

rows = consist.query_rows(
    "SELECT * FROM v_persons LIMIT 5",
    model=Persons,
    tracker=tracker,
)
df = consist.query_df("SELECT * FROM v_persons LIMIT 5", tracker=tracker)

Views automatically include Consist metadata columns (e.g. consist_run_id, consist_year, consist_scenario_id) for filtering and grouping.

items.title: Column Name Rules (Important)
items.text:
The generated stub aggressively normalizes attribute names to reduce runtime errors:

  • invalid characters become _
  • leading digits are prefixed with _
  • Python keywords get a trailing _
  • collisions become __2, __3, ...

When the attribute name differs from the real column name, the stub uses:

mass_kg: float | None = Field(default=None, sa_column=Column("Mass(kg)", ...))

This matters for views and empty-view typing: Consist now uses the original DB column name when creating typed empty views, so schemas with renamed attributes still behave correctly.

items.title: Matching Artifacts, Tables, and __tablename__
items.text:
For views to “pick up” your data, the model’s __tablename__ should match the concept key you are querying:

  • for ingested (“hot”) data, this is typically the DuckDB table name used at ingest time
  • for file-based (“cold”) data, this is typically the Artifact.key

If you want your curated model name to differ from the ingestion key, either:

  • override --table-name / table_name=... during export, or
  • set __tablename__ = "..." manually after editing

items.title: System and Ingestion Columns
items.text:
By default, exported stubs omit system/ingestion columns:

  • consist_* (Consist provenance columns)
  • _dlt_* (common ingestion/system columns)

Use --include-system-cols if you need a faithful “as-ingested” representation.

items.title: Wide / Sparse Tables
items.text:
Very wide tables can cause the stored JSON profile to truncate. Consist still persists per-field rows so schema export continues to work, and emits a warning when truncation occurs.

If your upstream workflow produces sparse wide tables, consider reshaping to a long format before ingestion or as a dedicated transformation step. Schema export is designed to keep working even when the summary JSON is truncated.

items.title: See Also
items.text:
• DLT Loader Integration Guide — Ingesting tabular data so schemas are captured
  • Architecture: Data Virtualization — How hybrid views work
  • Data Storage and Ingestion Strategy

items.title: Troubleshooting Guide
items.text:
This guide is a symptom index: find the message or behavior, confirm the likely cause, then apply the shortest fix. For concept definitions, see Core Concepts. For deeper topic guides, see:

  • Container Integration
  • DLT Loader
  • Mounts & Portability
  • Database Maintenance
  • Historical Recovery

items.title: "I need to inspect or repair the provenance DB"
items.text:
Diagnosis: DB maintenance is safest when you snapshot before mutating and diagnose before deleting or merging anything.

Fix: Use the full runbook in Database Maintenance. The short sequence is:

consist db snapshot --out ./snapshots/provenance.pre-maintenance.duckdb --db-path ./provenance.duckdb
consist db inspect --db-path ./provenance.duckdb
consist db doctor --db-path ./provenance.duckdb

Then take one action at a time: consist db purge --dry-run, consist db merge, consist db rebuild, and finally consist db compact.

items.title: "Database locked"
items.text:
Diagnosis: DuckDB allows only one writer at a time. Concurrent Consist processes can collide during run, artifact, or dlt sync writes.

Fix: Prefer sequential writes or separate DB files per process. On shared HPC filesystems, tune retries before redesigning the workflow:

export CONSIST_DLT_LOCK_RETRIES=40
export CONSIST_DLT_LOCK_BASE_SLEEP_SECONDS=0.2
export CONSIST_DLT_LOCK_MAX_SLEEP_SECONDS=5.0
export CONSIST_DB_LOCK_RETRIES=40
export CONSIST_DB_LOCK_BASE_SLEEP_SECONDS=0.2
export CONSIST_DB_LOCK_MAX_SLEEP_SECONDS=5.0

items.title: "unexpected keyword argument 'hash_inputs'"
items.text:
Diagnosis: hash_inputs is no longer accepted on run(...), trace(...), or step-level scenario execution surfaces.

Fix: Use identity_inputs=[...]. Scenario header contexts still route through begin_run(...), where hash_inputs remains a legacy low-level option.

items.title: "unexpected keyword argument 'config_plan'"
items.text:
Diagnosis: config_plan is no longer accepted on run(...), trace(...), or step-level scenario execution surfaces.

Fix: Pass adapter=... and optional identity_inputs=[...]. Scenario headers do not currently support header-level adapter=....

items.title: "identity_inputs/hash_inputs must be a list of paths."
items.text:
Diagnosis: A scalar string/path or invalid shape was passed where Consist expects a list.

Fix: Pass identity_inputs=[Path(...)] or identity_inputs=[("label", Path(...))].

items.title: "Failed to compute identity input digests ..."
items.text:
Diagnosis: One or more identity input paths are missing or unreadable.

Fix: Verify that each path exists and is readable before starting the run.

items.title: "load_inputs=True requires inputs to be a dict." / "input_binding=... requires inputs to be a dict."
items.text:
Diagnosis: Automatic input binding needs named inputs so Consist can match function parameters.

Fix: Pass inputs={"param_name": path_or_artifact}. To disable binding, use ExecutionOptions(input_binding="none").

items.title: "cache_hydration='outputs-requested' requires output_paths."
items.text:
Diagnosis: Requested-output hydration needs explicit destination mappings.

Fix: Declare output_paths={...} whenever using cache_hydration="outputs-requested".

items.title: "Tracker.run supports executor='python' or 'container'."
items.text:
Diagnosis: The executor value is not supported.

Fix: Use ExecutionOptions(executor="python") or ExecutionOptions(executor="container", container={...}).

items.title: "cache_options.code_identity callable modes require executor='python'."
items.text:
Diagnosis: Callable code identity modes require Python callable execution.

Fix: Switch to executor="python" or use code_identity="repo_git" for container runs.

items.title: "executor='container' requires output_paths."
items.text:
Diagnosis: Container runs cannot infer outputs from Python return values.

Fix: Provide explicit output mappings with output_paths={key: path}.

items.title: "Scenario input string did not resolve ..."
items.text:
Diagnosis: The string matched neither a Coupler key nor an existing filesystem path.

Fix: Pass a real path, or use consist.refs(...) between scenario steps on the preferred execution path.

items.title: "Consist has N active DuckDB relations..."
items.text:
Diagnosis: Relations returned by consist.load(...) for tabular artifacts keep a DuckDB connection open until closed.

Fix: Prefer consist.load_df(...) when a pandas DataFrame is enough, or use consist.load_relation(...) as a context manager. For intentional high fan-out, raise CONSIST_RELATION_WARN_THRESHOLD.

items.title: "Old DBs no longer load after the Relation-first refactor"
items.text:
Diagnosis: The artifact schema changed: uri became container_uri, child artifacts now use first-class table_path, array_path, and parent_artifact_id fields, and meta["table_path"] is no longer canonical.

Fix: Reset old local DBs and re-run workflows:

rm ./provenance.duckdb
rm ./test_db.duckdb

Then update code to use artifact.container_uri, artifact.table_path, and artifact.parent_artifact_id. Use tracker.get_child_artifacts(...) and tracker.get_parent_artifact(...) for container traversal.

items.title: "Cache hit but output files are missing"
items.text:
Diagnosis: Consist found matching provenance metadata, but default cache hits do not copy bytes back to disk.

Fix: Opt into hydration:

from consist import CacheOptions

result = tracker.run(
    fn=my_function,
    inputs={...},
    outputs=["results"],
    cache_options=CacheOptions(cache_hydration="outputs-all"),
)

For a prior run, archive mirror, or restart workspace, use tracker.hydrate_run_outputs(...); see Historical Recovery.

items.title: "I want to know why this run missed cache"
items.text:
Diagnosis: cache_hit=False means the signature did not match, but the reason is recorded on the completed run.

Fix: Inspect run.meta["cache_miss_explanation"]:

run = tracker.get_run("my_run_id")
explanation = run.meta.get("cache_miss_explanation", {})

print(explanation.get("reason"))
print(explanation.get("candidate_run_id"))
print(explanation.get("details", {}))

Use reason, candidate_run_id, matched_components, mismatched_components, and details to identify config, input, code, or candidate-output drift.

items.title: "Same inputs/config but cache not found"
items.text:
Diagnosis: A cache-key component changed. Common causes are code changes, config type drift such as 0 versus 0.0, changed input fingerprints, changed model / year / iteration, or dependency changes.

Fix: Compare the run's identity_summary and run.meta["cache_miss_explanation"]. For manual checks, compute the relevant code, config, and input hashes with tracker.identity.

For action-v2 runs, inspect identity_summary["input_identity"]["bindings"][*]["evidence"] to see whether a binding used verified content or a provenance fallback and why. If a run hit cache, identity_summary["cache"]["source_run_id"] identifies the earlier execution that supplied its outputs; compare that run's input links with the requested run's links when the same content came from a different producer occurrence.

items.title: "How do I clear/reset cache?"
items.text:
Diagnosis: You either want to remove all history or keep history while forcing one run to execute again.

Fix: Delete the DB only when you want a full reset:

rm ./provenance.duckdb

To keep history but force execution, use CacheOptions(cache_mode="overwrite").

items.title: "Container runs but /inputs is empty"
items.text:
Diagnosis: A host mount path does not exist, is relative when Docker needs an absolute path, or is unreadable.

Fix: Verify host paths with Path(...).exists(), pass absolute mount paths, check permissions, and debug with a direct docker run -v ... ls command. If Consist rejects paths outside configured mounts, add the mount to the Tracker or pass strict_mounts=False to run_container().

items.title: "URI resolution failed"
items.text:
Diagnosis: The URI scheme is unknown, the mount was not registered, or the artifact points at bytes that are no longer reachable from this machine.

Fix: Register the mount, fix the URI scheme, or hydrate from a recovery root. For portable path rules, see Mounts & Portability.

items.title: "Working directory changed between runs"
items.text:
Diagnosis: Relative paths were resolved from different working directories, so the recorded provenance path no longer points at the same bytes.

Fix: Prefer tracker-managed output paths, absolute mount-backed paths, or configured mount roots. For archived historical bytes, record artifact.meta["recovery_roots"] instead of depending on a mutable cwd.

items.title: "Schema mismatch during ingestion"
items.text:
Diagnosis: The file columns, dtypes, or table layout changed after the first ingest or no longer match the expected schema.

Fix: Inspect the actual file, schema metadata, and dlt loader logs. For loader-specific cases, see DLT Loader.

items.title: "Null in non-optional field"
items.text:
Diagnosis: Input data contains nulls where the table schema requires a value.

Fix: Clean or fill the source data before ingestion, or update the schema if null is a valid domain value.

items.title: "Duplicate primary keys"
items.text:
Diagnosis: The source table has repeated keys for a field Consist or the loader treats as unique.

Fix: Deduplicate upstream or change the declared key. Do not suppress the error until you know whether duplicate rows are legitimate.

items.title: "Can't query across runs"
items.text:
Diagnosis: The target records were never ingested, live in a different DB, or use incompatible schema/table names.

Fix: Confirm the run IDs in the active DB, inspect artifact metadata, and query only ingested tables or relations opened through Consist.

items.title: "Container execution failed"
items.text:
Diagnosis: The image, command, environment, mount, or output contract failed.

Fix: Re-run the equivalent docker run command with the same mounts and environment, then compare the container's expected outputs against output_paths.

items.title: "Output files not found after container"
items.text:
Diagnosis: The container completed but did not write the declared files where Consist expected them.

Fix: Check the container working directory, mount targets, file names, and permissions. Container runs must declare explicit output_paths.

items.title: "Image pull failed"
items.text:
Diagnosis: The registry, tag, credentials, or network path is unavailable.

Fix: Pull the image manually first, verify credentials, and pin an available tag for reproducible workflow runs.

items.title: "Permission denied in container"
items.text:
Diagnosis: The container user cannot read inputs or write mounted outputs.

Fix: Adjust host permissions, write to a mounted output directory owned by the executing user, or configure the container user to match the host workflow.

items.title: "Runs are very slow"
items.text:
Diagnosis: Slow runs usually come from hashing large inputs, copying cached outputs, container startup, DB contention, or expensive fallback recovery.

Fix: Check which phase is slow. Use narrower identity_inputs, avoid unneeded cache hydration, reduce concurrent DB writers, and hydrate only the keys you need.

items.title: "Database is huge and slow"
items.text:
Diagnosis: Old runs, ingested data, cache entries, or un-compacted deletes are accumulating.

Fix: Follow Database Maintenance: snapshot, inspect, purge with --dry-run, optionally prune cache where references are derivable, then compact.
