items.title: Command Instrumentation: Product Direction and Market Exploration
items.text:
Status: internal product exploration; no implementation decision

Decision to explore: Whether Consist should offer a low-friction CLI that runs an arbitrary terminal command while recording an explicit provenance boundary, and whether this should precede broad shared-artifact-registry work.
path: Command Instrumentation: Product Direction and Market Exploration

items.title: Executive view
items.text:
consist exec has a credible chance to be Consist's strongest adoption wedge. It gives a scientist useful, durable provenance without requiring them to turn a working script into a Python callable, write a workflow graph, or first adopt a shared catalog. The user declares the inputs and outputs that matter, Consist runs the command, and the resulting record is immediately searchable, hash bound, and lineage-capable.

The user-facing pitch is: prefix the command you already run with consist exec, declare what goes in and what must come out, and receive a verified, searchable record—plus a clear answer to what changed since the last named run—without a refactor, DAG, or pipeline file.

This is deliberately not a claim that arbitrary shell commands can be made fully reproducible by observation alone. A command wrapper should make the declared boundary trustworthy, preserve its limits, and provide a path into the existing Tracker.run(...), container, recovery, and future registry surfaces.

The publication-facing honesty sentence should be equally direct: Consist records what users declare and verifies declared results; it does not guess complete dependency capture. This keeps the internal pilot useful without overclaiming automatic reproducibility in JOSS or conference material.

The proposed prioritization is:

  1. Validate command instrumentation as an adoption wedge.
  2. Use explicit artifact roles/names in recorded runs to discover the registry semantics people actually repeat.
  3. Build shared registry capabilities only when cross-run discovery, aliasing, custody, or handoff are demonstrated needs.

This sequencing serves the current product goals of low-friction developer experience and a lightweight provenance layer. It does not replace the registry roadmap; it gives the registry high-quality, real usage evidence and an easier on-ramp.
path: Command Instrumentation: Product Direction and Market Exploration

items.title: Proposed user experience
items.text:
The initial shape should feel like a normal command invocation with an explicit provenance envelope:

consist exec \
  --name nc-baseline \
  --input config=configs/baseline.yaml \
  --input population=data/population.parquet \
  --outputs-dir outputs/ \
  --cwd . \
  -- python launch_model.py --config configs/baseline.yaml

On success, Consist should create a run record and input/output artifact links. It should emit a compact machine-readable execution record, for example under the selected run directory, plus normal CLI-readable run and lineage records. The final terminal summary should name the run ID, state that every declared output was present and recorded, compare it with the most recent successful run of the same name in the same project, and print one next inspection command: consist show <run-id>. The comparison must name its baseline run ID and say which of command/configuration, declared inputs, and declared outputs changed; it must never imply that a same name means equivalent scientific intent.

--outputs-dir is an explicit output-boundary declaration, not process tracing. It records the regular files newly created or modified beneath that directory by their relative paths, using a manifest/logical-output representation where appropriate. It does not infer reads, watch unrelated directories, or silently collect arbitrary filesystem changes. --output key=PATH remains the precise option for one named product.

Before committing a costly command, users can inspect the boundary without creating a run or spawning a child process:

consist exec --dry-run \
  --input config=configs/baseline.yaml \
  --outputs-dir outputs/ \
  -- python launch_model.py --config configs/baseline.yaml

The dry-run report must show the resolved argv and working directory, each input's fingerprint, the expected output boundary, code-identity mode, any warnings or unresolved paths, and the selected comparison baseline when one exists. Existing regular-file argv tokens should appear as suggested inputs only. They affect neither identity nor lineage unless the user explicitly names them with --input or promotes the displayed set with --accept-suggested. Suggestions must exclude the executable, -/stdin, URLs, and paths that are already declared as outputs; shell-mode commands receive no inferred inputs.

The command boundary must use argv execution after --, not construct a shell string. An explicit --shell mode is available for pipelines, redirection, and shell expansion, but it must be loud: record the script string, resolved shell executable, and shell=true in the run; warn that argv-level input suggestions are unavailable; and never silently change the default parsing or quoting semantics.
path: Command Instrumentation: Product Direction and Market Exploration

items.title: MVP bootstrap: a stable local project home
items.text:
consist init should create a minimal .consist/ project home with the local tracker and run-record locations. From any subdirectory, Consist should walk upward to the nearest .consist/ directory; explicit tracker/run-directory arguments still take precedence. The CLI must report the resolved project root in --dry-run and consist show output so users do not have to guess where a record was stored.

This is deliberately a marker and discovery rule, not a configuration language: no profiles, command recipes, environment policy, or implicit artifacts belong in the MVP. It removes routine tracker-location friction while retaining an unambiguous local provenance ledger for terminal and Python work.
path: Command Instrumentation: Product Direction and Market Exploration

items.title: Deferred post-pilot: project configuration and convention discovery
items.text:
Only after the bootstrap has been tested should Consist add a configuration file. Pilot evidence must show that repeated operational flags—not incorrect artifact declarations—are the material adoption obstacle.

Command instrumentation needs a project-level convention so that terminal commands and Python code join the same local provenance ledger without every invocation repeating database, run-directory, and policy flags. Support both a language-neutral .consist.toml and [tool.consist] in pyproject.toml; prefer the former in mixed-language repositories.

# .consist.toml
version = 1

[tracker]
db_path = ".consist/provenance.duckdb"
run_dir = ".consist/runs"

[identity]
code_root = "."
require_git = false

[commands]
log_retention = "on-failure"
environment_allowlist = ["PATH", "LANG", "OMP_NUM_THREADS"]
default_output_policy = "require-present"

[profiles.cluster]
run_dir = "/scratch/${USER}/my-project/consist-runs"
environment_allowlist = ["SLURM_JOB_ID", "OMP_NUM_THREADS"]

The corresponding Python entrypoint should be explicit and small:

from consist import open_project_tracker

tracker = open_project_tracker()

consist exec and open_project_tracker() must resolve the same effective configuration. The intended precedence is:

explicit CLI/API arguments
→ explicit --config / CONSIST_CONFIG
→ .consist.local.toml (ignored, machine-specific)
→ .consist.toml (committed project convention)
→ [tool.consist] in pyproject.toml

Resolve relative paths against the selected config file, never against the caller's current directory. Provide consist config show --resolved to display the effective non-secret configuration and which source supplied each value.
path: Command Instrumentation: Product Direction and Market Exploration

items.title: Configuration is not scientific identity
items.text:
The project config establishes operational convention: tracker location, run directory, mounts, profiles, log policy, and a safe environment allow-list. It must not silently become a cache input or define a second workflow language. Each run independently records the identity-bearing facts: declared input hashes, exact argv, command-specific configuration files, code identity, and selected environment digest. A profile change can be recorded as execution metadata; it changes the result identity only when it changes one of those declared inputs or execution facts.

Keep commands limited to defaults and policy. Do not add named command recipes, dependency inference, or implicit outputs in this config. Those would recreate a workflow DSL and blur the explicit boundary that makes the feature trustworthy.
path: Command Instrumentation: Product Direction and Market Exploration

items.title: What Consist would record
path: Command Instrumentation: Product Direction and Market Exploration

items.title: Required v1 facts
items.text:
• Exact argv list, working directory, start/end timestamps, duration, process exit status, and signal/termination outcome when available.
  • Declared input paths and output paths, their role keys, and the applicable content or manifest fingerprints.
  • Code identity when it can be established safely: repository revision and dirty state, or an explicit identity mode that says it was unavailable. It must not invent caller identity for a non-Python command.
  • A selected, allow-listed environment identity as a digest rather than raw secret-bearing environment values.
  • Paths to captured stdout/stderr files, with truncation/retention policy made explicit.
  • Post-exit output checks. Exit zero alone is not enough: a declared output must exist and pass the normal artifact admission/hash step before the run becomes successful.
  • An interruption outcome. The wrapper must record its best observed child signal/exit state on Ctrl-C and leave an actionable, reconcilable running record if the wrapper itself is killed before finalization.
  • The comparison baseline (or its absence), its run ID, and field-level classifications for command/configuration, declared inputs, and declared outputs. A comparison is evidence for inspection, not an equivalence claim.
path: Command Instrumentation: Product Direction and Market Exploration

items.title: Declared in-place mutation: simulation checkpoints and persistent stores
items.text:
Legacy tools and complex simulations frequently update a persistent store or checkpoint file at the same path that they consume. A prime example is simulation checkpoint-resume workflows (such as ActivitySim's cli_resume mode), where a base execution initializes a multi-gigabyte pipeline store (pipeline.h5 or pipeline.parquet), and subsequent calibration or continuation steps run resume_after by updating that store in place.

Without explicit mutation tracking, client harnesses are forced to write bespoke pre- and post-execution inspection logic to hash internal checkpoint tables or make defensive copies of large files. Consist provides a clean, native provenance shape for this pattern via explicit declared mutation:

consist exec \
  --input config=configs/baseline.yaml \
  --mutate pipeline=outputs/pipeline.h5 \
  -- python -m activitysim run -c configs -d data -o outputs --resume-after trip_mode_choice

In the Python API, tracker.exec(...) accepts mutate mappings alongside inputs and outputs:

result = tracker.exec(
    name="resume_simulation",
    argv=[
        "python", "-m", "activitysim", "run",
        "-c", "configs", "-d", "data", "-o", "outputs",
        "--resume-after", "trip_mode_choice",
    ],
    inputs={"config": "configs/settings.yaml"},
    mutate={"pipeline": "outputs/pipeline.h5"},
    outputs={"final_trips": "outputs/final_trips.csv"},
)

--mutate key=PATH (or mutate={"key": PATH}) means Consist requires and fingerprints the pre-state before spawn, then fingerprints and logs the post-state as a fresh output artifact after successful exit. The two records share a logical role key and URI but represent distinct, immutable artifact records in the provenance ledger:

run_042
  input   pipeline (pre-state)  → artifact A (before fingerprint)
  output  pipeline (post-state) → artifact B (after fingerprint)

This remains true even when the store bytes are unchanged: Consist creates a fresh output artifact record and deduplicates identical content separately in storage. It reports that case as pipeline: unchanged (<fingerprint>), not as an absent output or silent no-op. The command must reject a path simultaneously declared with --input and --output; --mutate is the unambiguous intent declaration.

Rules for mutation tracking:

  • The target must exist before launch. Creation belongs to --output; do not add --mutate-may-create in the initial increment.
  • Use full content fingerprints for the transition in the first increment. Fast structural or table-level digests (e.g. for HDF5 groups or Parquet partitions) may be layered in later via driver-specific plugins, but must never be presented as byte-transition evidence without a verified contract.
  • Acquire an exclusive advisory lock for the target and fail before spawn when it cannot be acquired. Do not pretend a before/after hash comparison can detect an interleaving writer; it cannot.
  • A deleted or unreadable post-state is treated as a failed declared output.
  • Generic host-command caching remains disabled. A future safe mutation cache would have to restore the exact pre-state in an isolated workspace and control publication of the post-state.

The existing run-to-artifact link key does not need to change for this design: the pre-state and post-state are separate artifact rows. The existing same-artifact input/output conflict check in Consist remains a useful guard against callers accidentally reusing one in-memory artifact reference.
path: Command Instrumentation: Product Direction and Market Exploration

items.title: Explicitly deferred facts
items.text:
• Automatic discovery of every read and written file.
  • Dependency installation, sandboxing, containerization, or a claim of bit-for-bit replayability.
  • Cache reuse by default.
  • Automatic parsing of a model's semantic configuration or performance metrics.
  • A shared registry, remote service, or artifact custody transfer.

These are not omissions to conceal. They are the feature's honesty contract: the user attests to the computational boundary, and Consist verifies and records it.
path: Command Instrumentation: Product Direction and Market Exploration

items.title: Selling points
path: Command Instrumentation: Product Direction and Market Exploration

items.title: Immediate value for scientists and modelers
items.text:
1. Preserve a working workflow. Record a legacy Python, R, Julia, Java, C++, shell, or vendor executable without first refactoring it into a library API. This matters particularly for research models that are expensive or risky to restructure.
  2. Turn a terminal command into evidence. A successful run is tied to declared input bytes, expected outputs, the command, and an execution outcome—not merely a notebook cell, a shell history line, or a directory timestamp.
  3. Recover lineage when the workflow is only partly formalized. Once a few commands have explicit inputs and outputs, consist lineage, run search, and artifact validation become useful even before there is a DAG.
  4. Meet multi-language and black-box tools at their natural boundary. The value applies equally to a simulator binary, an R analysis, an Apptainer launch, a shell script, or a Python program.
  5. Avoid secret and path leakage by design. Store a scrubbed/digested environment identity and explicit logs, instead of indiscriminately copying process state.
  6. Catch plausible-looking failures. A command that exits zero but omits a declared metrics.parquet is a failed run with a visible reason, rather than a result silently lost in shell history.
path: Command Instrumentation: Product Direction and Market Exploration

items.title: Product and adoption value
items.text:
1. A short time-to-first-value path. The first useful interaction is a single prefixed command, not an API migration or workflow rewrite.
  2. A natural bridge to existing Consist value. Recorded outputs can use the same artifact hashing, validation, recovery, querying, and portable lineage constructs that native runs use.
  3. A credible upgrade path. A repeated command can later become a native Tracker.run(...) wrapper, a container run, a scenario step, or a promoted registry artifact without losing prior provenance.
  4. Better product discovery than registry-first design. Repeated names, roles, output types, and handoff patterns expose which registry aliases and policies users actually need.
path: Command Instrumentation: Product Direction and Market Exploration

items.title: Strong use cases
items.text:
Use case Why the wrapper is strong What the user declares Legacy regional model launch The model remains a script/binary with file-oriented inputs and outputs; refactoring risks changing behavior. Config, prepared demand/network inputs, output directory or named final products. Calibration or parameter sweep trial Each trial needs comparison and provenance, but a full workflow engine is too much for an exploratory loop. Baseline inputs, parameter/config file, trial metrics and diagnostics. Simulation calibration with config overrides (ActivitySim, MATSim, EnergyPlus) Simulations run as CLI commands against dynamically overridden YAML/CSV parameter sets; requires materializing config overlays into CLI flags without custom subprocess wrappers. Base config dirs, parameter overrides, data directory, declared outputs (e.g. final_trips.csv). R/Julia/Stata/SAS analysis Native Consist decorators are not an option, but data-to-report provenance still matters. Input tables, script, rendered report and result tables. Container or HPC launcher The outer command launches a container or scheduler submission; Consist can record the intended boundary and submitted-job evidence. Image reference, launch config, submission record; final outputs only when completion is observed. Published-result reconstruction A user reruns one narrow analysis step and needs a defensible record without adopting an entire original pipeline. Source data/config, command, regenerated figure/table. Checkpoint-resume simulation & store mutation (ActivitySim pipeline.h5, MATSim events) Simulation continuation steps update an existing pipeline or state store in place; copying multi-gigabyte stores obscures lineage and wastes disk. Config plus an explicit --mutate target (e.g. pipeline=outputs/pipeline.h5); Consist records the before-to-after transition. Cross-repo handoff preparation A producer can make a named, verified output discoverable before a shared registry exists. Source artifacts, handoff manifest, promoted output candidates.

The less suitable cases are equally important: interactive GUI work; commands whose meaningful effects are hidden remote database mutations; long-running scheduler submissions whose completion cannot be observed by the local wrapper; and workflows where users need automatic scheduling, dynamic fan-out, or global DAG optimization. Those need adapters or workflow engines, not a misleading single-command abstraction.
path: Command Instrumentation: Product Direction and Market Exploration

items.title: Mixed-shape composition: Python, commands, and existing Consist applications
items.text:
Command instrumentation must compose with native Consist steps through one run/artifact model. The public API should therefore be tracker.exec(...) and scenario.exec(...); consist exec is a thin frontend over the same command executor, lifecycle, output admission, recovery, and lineage implementation.

Scenario: baseline
├── Python run: prepare inputs        (cacheable)
├── Command exec: run simulator       (record-only in v1)
└── Python run: validate and summarize (cacheable)

with tracker.scenario("baseline", model="regional_model") as sc:
    prepared = sc.run(
        prepare_inputs,
        inputs={"raw": raw_input},
        outputs=["prepared"],
    )

    simulation = sc.exec(
        name="simulate",
        argv=["./model", "--config", "configs/baseline.yaml"],
        inputs={"prepared": consist.ref(prepared, "prepared")},
        output_sets={"model_outputs": model_output_set},
        execution_options=CommandExecutionOptions(cwd=workspace),
    )

    sc.run(
        summarize,
        inputs={"outputs": consist.ref(simulation, "model_outputs")},
        outputs=["report"],
    )

Every independently meaningful computation is a sibling step under the scenario header. Artifact references, not raw output paths, express the producer-to-consumer lineage; path staging remains an explicit runtime concern when an external tool requires a fixed filename. Native Python run(...) steps retain their existing per-step cache semantics. Generic command steps are record-only until a later cache contract is designed.
path: Command Instrumentation: Product Direction and Market Exploration

items.title: Four composition shapes
items.text: Shape Representation Why A Python step calls a small helper command, such as a renderer or converter One run(...); store a bounded subprocess observation in its execution metadata. The Python function remains the meaningful computation. Adding a run node for every helper command creates lineage noise. A command has distinct inputs, outputs, substantial runtime, or reuse value scenario.exec(...) as a sibling Python/command step. The command has a real provenance boundary, with its own exit status, logs, and artifacts. A command requires materialized configuration overrides (e.g. simulation calibration) tracker.exec_with_config_overrides(...) Evaluates an external CLI simulator against dynamically materialized config overlays without custom subprocess wrappers. A terminal-launched Python application already instruments internal work with Consist Delegated execution envelope plus child native runs. Captures terminal facts without duplicating the internal application's step lineage.
path: Command Instrumentation: Product Direction and Market Exploration

items.title: Composition with configuration adapters and overrides (tracker.exec_with_config_overrides)
items.text:
In simulation calibration, parameter sweeps, and sensitivity analysis (e.g., ActivitySim, MATSim, EnergyPlus), models are executed as CLI processes, not Python callables. In calibration loops, each trial evaluates a candidate parameter vector (such as mode choice coefficients or model constants). Consist already provides domain configuration adapters (ConfigAdapter, ActivitySimConfigAdapter, ConfigOverrides) to parse YAML/CSV configurations, compute canonical config hashes, and materialize overrides into isolated overlay directories.

However, tracker.run_with_config_overrides(...) assumes the target is a Python callable (fn). Client code in activitysim-calibration was therefore forced to write hundreds of lines of custom subprocess wrapping (subprocess.run, stderr/stdout capture, exit code inspection, path reconciliation) in runner.py and _evaluate_real_activitysim_step just to connect materialized configuration directories to CLI invocations.

Consist bridges this gap by composing command execution directly with configuration adapters:

result = tracker.exec_with_config_overrides(
    adapter=adapter,
    base_config_dirs=[config_dir],
    overrides=overrides,
    command=[
        "python", "-m", "activitysim", "run",
        "-c", "{selected_root_dir}",
        "-c", "{base_config_dirs[0]}",
        "-d", "{data_dir}",
        "-o", "{output_dir}",
    ],
    template_vars={
        "data_dir": data_dir,
        "output_dir": workspace / "output",
    },
    inputs={"data": data_dir},
    outputs={"final_trips": "output/final_trips.csv"},
    mutate={"pipeline": "output/pipeline.h5"},  # optional checkpoint resume
)
path: Command Instrumentation: Product Direction and Market Exploration

items.title: Lifecycle and Semantics
items.text:
1. Config Canonicalization & Override Materialization: Consist canonicalizes the base configuration roots and writes the overridden parameters into a managed overlay directory (matching run_with_config_overrides).
  2. Dynamic Argv Template Substitution: Consist replaces declared placeholder tokens in the command argv list:
  3. {selected_root_dir}: The path to the materialized overlay configuration directory.
  4. {root_dirs}: The ordered list of all configuration roots (materialized overlay directory followed by base directories).
  5. {materialized_dir}: Alias for {selected_root_dir}.
  6. Any keys supplied in template_vars.
  7. Command Execution: Consist delegates execution to CommandExecutor, managing working directory, environment filtering, process group isolation, and bounded stdout/stderr logging.
  8. Declared Artifact Checks & Mutation Capture: On zero process exit, Consist verifies that declared outputs (such as final_trips.csv) exist, computes post-state fingerprints for declared --mutate targets (such as pipeline.h5), and admits them into the provenance ledger.
  9. Unified Provenance Record: Consist records a single run record binding:
  10. The canonical configuration identity and exact parameter override values (via the ConfigAdapter),
  11. The command execution facts (argv, working directory, exit status, duration, stdout/stderr retention),
  12. Input artifact digests, output artifact fingerprints, and pre/post mutation transitions.

This eliminates client-side subprocess runners entirely, decoupling model execution from the calibration orchestration loop while preserving complete provenance.
path: Command Instrumentation: Product Direction and Market Exploration

items.title: Deferred: delegated execution envelope
items.text:
Delegated mode is deliberately outside the first pilot, but it is the likely dogfooding path for terminal-launched applications that already use Consist internally, including PILATES-shaped workflows. The generic pilot must not exclude those users by implying this exists today; it should validate opaque command recording separately, then design delegation as its own security/lifecycle increment.

An already-instrumented application needs a distinct mode:

consist exec --delegate -- python pipeline.py --scenario baseline

The outer command run is an execution envelope. It owns argv, working directory, process outcome, selected environment identity, and log policy. It passes a short-lived, narrowly scoped execution-context reference to the child process. The child joins the configured project tracker and creates its normal scenario/run tree below that envelope:

tracker = consist.connect_execution_context()

with tracker.scenario("baseline") as sc:
    prepared = sc.run(...)
    results = sc.run(...)

The context handoff should identify the already-resolved tracker configuration, parent/envelope run ID, run-directory policy, and a capability that expires with the launch. It must not contain secrets or let an arbitrary process attach to an unrelated run. A child process may only join an active envelope selected by the parent, and the persisted record must identify this delegated relationship.

Delegated mode is intentionally not an opaque-output command run. The internal children own their outputs and cache identities. The envelope may present an aggregate summary or a separately named final handoff artifact, but it must not log the same physical outputs again under competing producers. This prevents duplicate artifacts, ambiguous lineage, and cache ownership errors.
path: Command Instrumentation: Product Direction and Market Exploration

items.title: Deferred: shared executor contract
items.text:
Do not refactor containers or existing Python execution into a new executor protocol to prove the adoption wedge. The prototype can implement a narrow tracker.exec(...) by using the existing run lifecycle around argv process execution. Once the pilot validates the command contract, consolidate the following execution surfaces only if doing so removes demonstrated duplication.

The target post-pilot shape is a shared ExecutionSpec / ExecutionResult and executor protocol rather than permanently maintaining a CLI-specific path:

  • PythonCallableExecutor backs existing run(...) behavior.
  • CommandExecutor owns argv process launch, bounded log capture, exit/status recording, and declared output checks.
  • Existing container execution becomes another executor implementation where appropriate, retaining its stronger image/mount identity contract.

All executors feed the same run creation, artifact admission, lifecycle hooks, lineage, recovery, and optional OpenLineage emission. This preserves one provenance universe while allowing the executor-specific facts to remain honest.
path: Command Instrumentation: Product Direction and Market Exploration

items.title: Deferred: terminal flow artifact routing
items.text:
Flow routing is a follow-on usability pilot, not a prerequisite for the first valid command record. Its priority should be decided by observed user friction: repeated flag setup, output declaration, or artifact handoff may prove more important first.

Successive terminal commands need the ergonomic equivalent of consist.ref(...), without turning paths or a mutable notion of “latest” into provenance. Introduce a scoped terminal flow with named artifact slots:

consist flow start baseline

consist exec \
  --publish prepared=work/prepared.parquet \
  -- python prepare.py --out work/prepared.parquet

consist exec \
  --input prepared=@flow:prepared \
  --stage prepared=work/inputs/prepared.parquet \
  --publish simulation=work/simulation/ \
  -- ./run-model --input work/inputs/prepared.parquet --out work/simulation/

consist exec \
  --input simulation=@flow:simulation \
  --stage simulation=work/inputs/simulation \
  --publish report=work/report.html \
  -- python summarize.py --inputs work/inputs/simulation --out work/report.html

The selected flow is a scenario-like parent record plus a small durable flow-manifest. Each successful --publish adds a slot binding:

flow baseline
  prepared   → (producing run, artifact ID, content hash)
  simulation → (producing run, artifact ID, manifest-v1 identity)
  report     → (producing run, artifact ID, content hash)

@flow:prepared is a convenience selector only. Before execution it resolves to the exact producing run, artifact ID, and verified file/directory manifest; the consuming run persists that resolved reference as its input lineage. The flow alias itself is not the input identity. Therefore later inspection and replay retain the precise bytes consumed even if the slot is subsequently rebound.

--stage deliberately separates logical identity from the workspace path a tool needs. It uses the normal materialization/hydration rules to place the selected artifact at an explicit destination. This avoids treating a raw path as proof of provenance and keeps fixed-filename tools practical.
path: Command Instrumentation: Product Direction and Market Exploration

items.title: Flow rules
items.text:
• Flow aliases are local to one named flow, not global registry aliases and not a remote custody claim.
  • The initial concept uses single-assignment slots with explicit --replace-slot NAME, retaining the old binding in append-only history. The follow-on pilot must test retries and parameter sweeps before freezing this UX: a keyed/iteration-scoped publication form may be safer than repeatedly overwriting one canonical slot.
  • Resolve collisions, missing slots, ambiguous artifact keys, and failed materialization before spawning the command.
  • The default selector must never mean “the prior command” or “latest matching output.” Those become wrong after retries, parallel work, or multi-output steps.
  • An interactive shell may activate a flow through a short-lived environment variable, but --flow FLOW_ID must work in scripts and CI. The durable manifest, not shell state, is authoritative.
  • A flow should expose its exact bindings through consist flow show and let consist show/lineage traverse each resulting ordinary run.

This is deliberately a thin routing convenience, not a workflow DSL. It has no implicit dependency inference, scheduling, fan-out, retry policy, or cache policy. It makes terminal composition explicit while preserving the same artifact contract used by Python scenarios.
path: Command Instrumentation: Product Direction and Market Exploration

items.title: Competitive landscape
items.text:
This is a capability comparison, not a claim that Consist should displace these tools. Most competitors are excellent at their intended layer.

Category / examples What users get Where consist exec differs Product implication DVC Declarative stages with commands, dependencies, outputs, lockfiles, and reproduction/caching behavior. DVC's model is explicitly a pipeline/stage graph. Consist can record a command today without adding or maintaining a project pipeline definition, and can preserve richer local provenance/recovery semantics. Do not compete by recreating a DAG engine. Offer a path for commands that are not yet—or never should be—DVC stages. MLflow Projects and Tracking ML-focused project execution plus tracking of runs, parameters, metrics, code, and artifacts; projects can be invoked from local directories or Git URIs. MLflow is strongest when the user adopts its experiment/project model and logs ML-oriented metadata. Consist's niche is general scientific artifacts, explicit lineage, content identity, and non-ML tools. Avoid an ML metric dashboard race. Make the command wrapper valuable to a simulator or scientific analysis with no training loop. Snakemake / Nextflow Declarative workflow languages, scheduling, execution reports, and task-level provenance for established pipelines. They require a workflow description and manage task orchestration; Consist would instrument one pre-existing command without becoming the scheduler. Position the feature before formalization and at integration boundaries, not as a substitute for mature workflow engines. Kedro / Dagster Python-oriented pipeline/asset abstractions, catalogs, orchestration, and external-process integration. These frameworks own the pipeline model; Dagster can launch shell work inside its orchestration context. Consist should remain usable when there is no framework-owned project. Build optional emitters/adapters later rather than imitating framework architecture. Makefile plus README Lightweight command recipes and human-maintained notes, often adequate for a stable local workflow. Neither verifies that declared products exist after a run, fingerprints the exact input/output transition, or provides queryable lineage across reruns. Respect this as the low-complexity baseline; prove the added value with missing-output and changed-artifact evidence, not abstract provenance language. ReproZip System-call-level experiment tracing and packaging for later reproduction, including command line, working directory, and files. Its goal is a much heavier portable reproduction bundle. Consist should record an explicit, queryable provenance boundary and only archive/copy artifacts when requested. The closest conceptual precedent validates demand, while illustrating why v1 must resist automatic “capture everything” scope. OpenLineage A standard event model for job/run lifecycle and lineage; it is commonly emitted by orchestrators and integrations. It is an interchange/event contract, not a local command runner, artifact verifier, cache identity system, or recovery layer. Continue to treat OpenLineage as an optional outbound projection, not the execution core.
path: Command Instrumentation: Product Direction and Market Exploration

items.title: Relevant external evidence
items.text:
• DVC pipeline documentation describes stages through command, dependency, and output relationships; that is useful precisely because it is a maintained declarative graph, not an ad-hoc command recorder.
  • MLflow Projects provides a conventional project format and mlflow run for local or Git-based projects; MLflow Tracking organizes execution into runs with metadata and artifacts.
  • Snakemake reports and Nextflow trace observers demonstrate the reporting depth available once a workflow engine owns the task lifecycle.
  • Dagster's shell integration launches shell commands from an asset/orchestration context; it confirms the value of external-command boundaries but assumes Dagster ownership.
  • ReproZip's glossary describes tracing one or more command lines, while its unpacking documentation shows its deliberate emphasis on replay bundles and environment handling.
  • OpenLineage's specification defines lifecycle events for a run of a job. It is a useful interoperable emission target, not a substitute for Consist's local artifact contract.
path: Command Instrumentation: Product Direction and Market Exploration

items.title: Relationship to the object registry
items.text:
The two ideas solve different moments in the lifecycle.

Question Command instrumentation Shared object registry Primary user question “What exactly happened when I ran this?” “Which trusted artifact fills this role, where is it, and may I use it?” First value A single existing command. A community agrees on roles, identity, location, aliases, and admission rules. Authority Local execution record and explicit artifact links. Shared immutable identity, custody/admission evidence, durable locations, and alias policy. Main risk Overclaiming discovery or reproducibility. Premature governance and semantic commitments. Natural connection Declared output names/roles reveal registry candidates. Promoted artifacts can be fed back as explicit inputs to later command records.

Consist's portable provenance schema intentionally does not make itself an artifact registry or a complete execution-observation model. This proposal preserves that boundary: the CLI writes local execution and artifact evidence; it does not create a remote source of truth, grant a semantic alias, or claim custody. A future registry can promote only verified, explicitly selected artifacts from these records.
path: Command Instrumentation: Product Direction and Market Exploration

items.title: Product boundaries and hard questions
path: Command Instrumentation: Product Direction and Market Exploration

items.title: Avoid “magic file discovery” in v1
items.text: File-system tracing, process tracing, or before/after directory diffs cannot reliably determine semantic inputs and outputs. They miss remote reads, can collect enormous irrelevant trees, blur temporary files with products, and create security/privacy concerns. They are reasonable optional diagnostics only after the explicit-boundary workflow is valuable.
path: Command Instrumentation: Product Direction and Market Exploration

items.title: Separate synchronous execution from asynchronous submission
items.text: consist exec should initially mean that Consist observed the child process finish. sbatch, cloud submission, and queue APIs are separate adapters: record the submission as a submitted job, then attach completion/output evidence only after a monitor has observed it. A local zero exit from sbatch is not model success.
path: Command Instrumentation: Product Direction and Market Exploration

items.title: Start record-only, not cache-first
items.text:
The existing container path already has the right ingredients for a later cacheable command contract: exact argv, digested environment identity, declared inputs, and declared outputs. But a generic host command has more uncontrolled state than a container. A cache mode should remain off until a later design defines eligible identity modes, output recovery, mutation policy, and failure semantics.

For the internal pilot only, Consist may explore an explicit --reuse-if-verified no-op mode after the comparison contract is proven. It is not the default and not a public reproducibility claim. Before declining to spawn a command, it must verify exact command and code identity, declared-input fingerprints, and the existence and current fingerprints of every declared output against a prior successful run. It must name that prior run, record that it performed verification rather than execution, and require --force to run anyway. It performs no output restoration. Commands with undeclared external side effects remain ineligible by user attestation; this is deliberately a bounded internal reuse experiment, not generic caching under another name.
path: Command Instrumentation: Product Direction and Market Exploration

items.title: Treat logs as evidence with policy controls
items.text: Logs often include credentials, hostnames, user paths, and large duplicated output. Provide an explicit default retention limit, redaction hooks, and an opt-out. The run record must state whether output was retained, truncated, or omitted; absence must not look like a successful capture.
path: Command Instrumentation: Product Direction and Market Exploration

items.title: Interruptions and abandoned running records
items.text: The wrapper should create its running record before spawning the child, handle Ctrl-C by recording the observed interruption and forwarding termination according to a documented process-group policy, and finalize logs/output checks when it remains alive. It cannot reliably finalize if it is itself SIGKILLed or the host crashes. That residual running record must be visible to existing status-reconciliation tooling; the CLI should show the exact recovery command instead of treating it as a completed or failed observation without evidence.
path: Command Instrumentation: Product Direction and Market Exploration

items.title: Smallest credible MVP
path: Command Instrumentation: Product Direction and Market Exploration

items.title: In scope
items.text:
• consist init, a .consist/ project marker, and upward project discovery from nested working directories, while retaining explicit tracker and run-directory overrides.
  • A consist exec CLI command with --input key=PATH, --output key=PATH, --outputs-dir PATH, --name, --cwd, --dry-run, --accept-suggested, explicit --shell, and -- argv separation. --outputs-dir is the onboarding/default story; keyed --output is the precise downstream handle.
  • A narrow public tracker.exec(...) used by the CLI, built directly on the existing run lifecycle. Its command, keyed input/output boundaries, environment, and working-directory parameters should align with run_container(...) where their meanings overlap, without importing image, mount, backend, or cache semantics. scenario.exec(...) follows only after the command contract has passed the pilot.
  • A local Tracker lifecycle that creates a running record before spawn, captures process outcome/interruption, hashes declared inputs/outputs, and records stdout/stderr according to policy.
  • Success only when the command exits successfully and declared outputs pass existence/admission checks; exit zero with a missing declared output is a failed run.
  • A compact comparison to the prior successful run with the same project/name, identifying changes to command/configuration, declared inputs, and declared outputs and naming the baseline run ID.
  • Failure records that retain command and process evidence without admitting nonexistent or failed outputs.
  • JSON output suitable for scripts, plus normal runs, show, artifacts, lineage, and validate usability.
  • Focused docs led by a failed/missing-output and changed-baseline example, followed by R and Julia commands; include an output-directory command and a Python example, but do not lead with Python.
path: Command Instrumentation: Product Direction and Market Exploration

items.title: Out of scope
items.text:
• Full filesystem/process tracing, auto-capture of dependencies, scheduler completion monitoring, automatic caching, remote execution, registry promotion, DAG orchestration, a web dashboard, configuration-file discovery, profile resolution, shared executor refactoring, scenario.exec(...), declared mutation, or delegated context handoff. These designs are retained above as explicit post-pilot increments. The narrowly attested internal --reuse-if-verified experiment is not automatic caching and requires its own admission decision after the comparison pilot.
  • Flow-slot routing is a follow-on pilot after the one-command opaque-recording contract is proven; it is not needed to establish first-command value.
path: Command Instrumentation: Product Direction and Market Exploration

items.title: Validation plan before committing to implementation
items.text:
1. Design spike: build a narrow tracker.exec(...) on the existing run lifecycle, a minimal consist init, and upward .consist/ discovery, without a storage-schema migration, full configuration system, or executor refactor. Exercise R/Julia-like external executable fixtures, an output-directory command, a Python script, and an expected-output failure.
  2. Failure-first and comparison demonstration: make the expected-output failure a primary example: the process exits zero, metrics.parquet is absent, and Consist records the run as failed with the exact missing-output reason and a pointer to its logs. Then rerun a named command with one changed input/configuration and show the named baseline, changed field, and output result in the compact summary.
  3. Usability study: ask 5–8 target users to record a real command. Report the count who create a valid record, the time to first valid record, and each observed declaration failure mode; do not turn this small sample into a noisy percentage claim. Include nested-directory discovery, --outputs-dir, and suggested-input acceptance in the observed setup friction.
  4. Trust tests: verify quoting/argv preservation, no shell injection in the default mode; explicit-shell recording; nonzero exit capture; signal interruption; missing output; suggested-input exclusions and explicit promotion; comparison-baseline selection; secret-redaction behavior; dirty Git identity behavior; and wrapper interruption/orphan reconciliation.
  5. Internal reuse decision: only after the comparison tests pass, decide whether an internal --reuse-if-verified pilot is worth its separate contract. Test exact identity checks, output re-fingerprinting, explicit --force, a recorded no-op outcome, and rejection for un-attested external side effects. Do not present its results as a public cache guarantee.
  6. Mutation cost measurement: measure full pre/post hashing on representative simulation checkpoint stores (such as ActivitySim pipeline.h5 / pipeline.parquet from calibration resume trials). Verify transition artifact creation, advisory locking, and whether full SHA-256 digests remain performant on multi-gigabyte files.
  7. Config adapter & override execution test: validate tracker.exec_with_config_overrides with an external simulator CLI (such as ActivitySim). Assert overlay directory materialization, argv template interpolation (-c {selected_root_dir}), zero-exit checks, declared output admission (final_trips.csv), and single-record binding of config identity with command execution facts.
  8. Composition increment: only after opaque command recording passes, run a cacheable Python → command → cacheable Python scenario. Assert sibling parentage, exact artifact lineage, output-set admission, and that a command's record-only status does not disable reuse of adjacent native steps.
  9. Configuration increment: only if pilot evidence identifies repeated operational flags as real friction, test config discovery, precedence, relative-path anchoring, profiles, source reporting, and absence of accidental cache misses.
  10. Flow-routing pilot: after opaque recording passes, run a three-command terminal flow. Verify exact slot resolution, explicit staging, single-write slots, append-only replacement history, retry/parameter-sweep usability, parallel ambiguity failures, and ordinary artifact lineage from each consumer to its producer.
  11. Boundary tests: prove that no cache hit, global registry alias, remote publication, delegated child relationship, or “reproducible” claim appears from v1 records alone. A flow-local alias must never masquerade as a global semantic alias.
  12. Decision gate: proceed only if users can create accurate records for their real commands with little setup and the resulting lineage answers a question they otherwise could not answer from shell history and directories.
path: Command Instrumentation: Product Direction and Market Exploration

items.title: Success criteria
items.text:
The feature is promising if it achieves all of the following in a pilot:

  • Report how many of the 5–8 target users create one valid record for a real command without code changes, together with concrete declaration failures and the time to correct them.
  • Most pilot records have inputs and outputs that users later judge complete enough to explain the result; incompleteness is visibly represented rather than silently hidden.
  • Users use the compact named-run comparison to answer a concrete “what changed since the last baseline?” question, and at least two independently use show to inspect the cited run evidence.
  • The failure-first example demonstrates that a zero-exit command with a missing declared product is rejected rather than recorded as a successful result.
  • Users can find the same local tracker from a nested directory and can either declare or explicitly accept suggested input paths without mistaking a suggestion for automatic dependency capture.
  • At least one repeated role/name pattern provides concrete evidence for a registry alias or admission feature, rather than a hypothetical one.
  • No pilot user is misled into thinking Consist captured all dependencies, guaranteed replay, made a scheduler-submitted model run complete, or turned the internal reuse experiment into a general cache guarantee.
path: Command Instrumentation: Product Direction and Market Exploration

items.title: Decision requested after exploration
items.text:
Authorize a narrowly bounded, internal-first prototype and pilot, with the record-only contract above. Its public-facing JOSS and conference story is explicit boundaries, verified results, and named-run comparison—not automatic dependency capture or caching. Do not authorize registry expansion, generic caching, filesystem tracing, full configuration-file discovery, executor refactoring, terminal flows, declared mutation, or delegated execution as part of that prototype.

If the pilot passes the usability and trust gates, the next planning document should specify the public CLI contract, execution-record schema, log-retention policy, and migration path to the existing container and Tracker.run(...) implementations.
path: Command Instrumentation: Product Direction and Market Exploration

items.title: 1. Guiding Principles: Clean End State, Zero Split-Brain
items.text:
Because v0.5 will not be deployed to production mid-stack between PR 1 and PR 4—and existing v0.4 databases can be migrated cleanly via consist migrate—we optimize strictly for the cleanest, fastest, least-risky end state rather than carrying v0.4 runtime compatibility shims:

  1. Subtractive In-Place Replacement (One Mental Model):
  2. Every PR upgrades an existing v0.4.2 seam in place and deletes superseded v0.4.2 code in the same PR (including deleting src/consist/core/schema_compat.py's legacy v0.2/v0.3 runtime backfill shims).
  3. Never introduce a second persistence class (StoreLedger beside DatabaseManager), a second output/archive engine (engine.seal / PendingOutput beside Tracker), a second run JSON format (store/manifest.py beside consist.json), or a second identity type (AdmissionIdentity beside Digest).
  4. Clean ~14-Table v0.5 Schema + Cold-Safe consist migrate (~350–450 LOC, Not 5,786 LOC):
  5. Avoid both v0.4 runtime ALTER TABLE shims and PR #316's 21-table over-normalization (artifact_location_event append logs + ROW_NUMBER() CTE views + anchor_promotion joins + Kind.HISTORICAL / consist promote).
  6. Keep config_facet, run_config_kv, artifact_facet, and artifact_kv as direct indexed DuckDB tables populated via executemany (zero wrapper views, zero query rewrites across queries.py/views.py/pivot_facets).
  7. Store a clean consist_schema(version=2, db_uid=...) header; opening a version=1 DB raises DatabaseMigrationRequired("Run 'consist migrate <db_path>'") (subclassing IncompatibleSchemaError) immediately with zero legacy fallback branches in runtime code.
  8. consist migrate <db_path> applies deterministic rules safe for both hot local workspaces and cold/temporarily unmounted HPC archives:
    • Artifact bytes exist on disk (under --mounts / --run-dir): compute the canonical v0.5 Digest via its real scheme driver (or, with --trust-v04-hashes for multi-TB archives, convert already-attested 64-hex v0.4 SHA-256 / manifest-v1 / logical_matrices hashes without re-reading multi-TB files while always re-hashing non-hex fast hashes), capture FileStat (racy=False when older than 2s), insert an 'active' artifact_location row, and—when all inputs of a run have valid v0.5 Digests—recompute the run's native v0.5 input_hash and signature (cacheable=True -> 100% live cache hits immediately, fixing B15).
    • Artifact bytes missing or archive currently unmounted: record digest = None (preserving legacy_v04_hash in artifact.meta), still insert all recovery_roots + container_uri into artifact_location keyed by artifact_id (digest IS NULL) so mounting the archive later immediately restores art.path and cold ViewFactory reads, and mark linked runs cacheable = False. Copy global_tables.* and custom SQL views intact.
  9. Clean End-State Public Contracts:
  10. Artifact.digest: Digest | None, Artifact.uri: str, Artifact.member: str | None: Canonical scheme-qualified identity (digest.scheme, digest.hex, str(digest) == "<scheme>:<hex>") and single primary URI + optional container member, replacing untyped Artifact.hash and split container_uri/table_path/array_path.
  11. First-Class BaseModel / SQLModel User Row Schemas Without ORM Coupling: Consist's internal provenance models (Artifact, Run, etc.) are pure dataclasses / Pydantic models with zero SQLModel(table=True) or SQLAlchemy Session execution, while user-defined tabular row schemas (Tracker(schemas=[Person]), dlt strict mode, ViewFactory, ibis_view, schema_stub) stay first-class via pure Pydantic model_fields introspection.
  12. Explicit, Zero-Surprise Step Parameter Binding:
    • Parameter type annotations always take precedence (def step(x: Artifact): -> Artifact with zero pre-step staging/hydration I/O; def step(x: Path): -> verified staged Path with zero DataFrame load; def step(x: pd.DataFrame): / GeoDataFrame / xr.Dataset / pa.Table -> loaded dataset via consist.load; output out: Path -> injected target Path for outputs={"out": ...}).
    • Unannotated input parameters def step(x): default to Artifact (zero eager pre-step I/O, fixing B17), unless the caller explicitly specifies ExecutionOptions(input_binding="paths" | "loaded").
  13. Strict Acyclic Downward Dependency DAG (Zero Hidden Back-Edges):
  14. Layer 1 — Leaf (consist.digest, consist.types, consist.protocols): Stdlib + optional Arrow/Pandas/HDF5 only; zero imports from consist.models.* or consist.core.*. Defines ArtifactResolver protocol + contextvars active-resolver hook (get_active_resolver / bind_active_resolver).
  15. Layer 2 — Value Models & Witnesses (consist.models.artifact, consist.models.run, consist.location): Frozen/plain value objects + FileStat/DirTreeStat witnesses. Zero imports of Tracker or DatabaseManager; zero live SQL/I/O inside data fields (uri, digest, member, meta) or JSON serialization. Convenience resolution methods (art.path, art.as_path(), art.ensure_local_path(), art.as_df(), art.accessibility()) delegate strictly via weakref/contextvar ArtifactResolver (art.with_resolver(...) via dataclasses.replace—zero object.__setattr__!).
  16. Layer 3 — Persistence (DatabaseManager in consist.core.persistence): One class owning the native duckdb.DuckDBPyConnection, schema DDL, indexed SQL queries, cursor tracking, and dlt connection borrowing.
  17. Layer 4 — Workflow & Surface (Tracker, Coupler, TrackerArchiveService, materialize.py, ViewFactory, cli.py, api.py).
  18. Hard Merge Gates on Every PR:
  19. scripts/benchmarks/metadata_hot_path_profile.py (20-in / 15-out warm miss & cache.hit.start_run) <= 1.0x of origin/main (<= 235 ms / <= 245 ms), plus sub-millisecond art.path, Coupler.set, and Ephemeral Mode Tracker().
  20. Clean-venv smoke test (uv venv with base consist only—no consist[git], pandas >= 3.0, Python 3.11 & 3.13).
  21. Architectural & hygiene gates: zero new circular dependencies, zero post-init object.__setattr__ / getattr / .__dict__.get hacks on domain/tracker state, and typing_extensions.Protocol + typing_extensions.runtime_checkable across all @runtime_checkable protocols in src/consist/.

items.title: Design & Implementation Blueprint
items.text:
1. Single Native Connection, Poison-Safe Re-Entrant Transactions & Subprocess Barrier (DatabaseManager):
  2. Own one duckdb.DuckDBPyConnection (duckdb.connect(str(db_path), read_only=read_only)) guarded by self._lock = threading.RLock() and self._cond = threading.Condition(self._lock) (_suspended: bool).
  3. Re-entrant transactions without SAVEPOINT (DuckDB does not support SQL SAVEPOINT): track _tx_depth: int = 0 and _tx_poisoned: bool = False under self._lock:
    • _tx_depth 0 -> 1 executes BEGIN TRANSACTION.
    • _tx_depth > 1 joins the active transaction on self.connection without issuing SQL; if an inner with db.transaction(): exits via exception, set _tx_poisoned = True and re-raise. Exiting depth 1 -> 0 checks _tx_poisoned: if poisoned (even if an outer caller caught the inner exception), execute ROLLBACK and raise TransactionAbortedError rather than silently committing partial state. Use SELECT checks or ON CONFLICT instead of try/catch write probes inside transactions.
  4. Cursor visibility & lifecycle:
    • When _tx_depth > 0, execute all queries directly on self.connection under self._lock so nested helpers see uncommitted writes and never trigger DuckDB MVCC write-write conflicts.
    • When _tx_depth == 0, relation_query() clones a tracked cursor registered in self._open_cursors so to_df(..., close=True), db.close(), and suspend_for_subprocesses() reliably close the underlying root cursor even when callers chain .limit() / .filter() (which return new DuckDBPyRelation wrappers in DuckDB 1.5.1).
  5. suspend_for_subprocesses(): sets _suspended = True, closes all tracked cursors in self._open_cursors, closes any cached Ibis cursor backend (TrackerIbisIntegration.close()), executes CHECKPOINT + closes self.connection, and blocks any concurrent thread attempting DB access on self._cond until resumed.
  6. Schema header check: on open, inspect consist_schema.version; if version == 1 (or legacy unversioned run table), raise DatabaseMigrationRequired("Database uses Consist v0.4 schema (version=1). Run 'consist migrate <db_path>'.") (subclassing IncompatibleSchemaError).
  7. Clean Native DuckDB Tables (Zero Wrapper Views):
  8. Create core tables via explicit DuckDB SQL DDL:
    • consist_schema(version INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, db_uid VARCHAR NOT NULL, updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ)
    • run (including cacheable BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE, meta JSON, tags JSON, stage VARCHAR, phase VARCHAR, facet_id VARCHAR, etc.)
    • artifact(id UUID PRIMARY KEY, key VARCHAR NOT NULL, uri VARCHAR NOT NULL, driver VARCHAR NOT NULL, digest VARCHAR, member VARCHAR, run_id VARCHAR, parent_artifact_id UUID, facet_id VARCHAR, meta JSON, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ) (mapped cleanly to/from Artifact.container_uri, table_path/array_path, and hash inside DatabaseManager until PR 2 upgrades the Artifact class; artifact_content table removed)

items.title: Design & Implementation Blueprint
items.text:
1. Unified consist.digest Leaf Module & ArtifactResolver Protocol (consist.protocols):
  2. Extend existing src/consist/digest.py (1,777 LOC on origin/main owning canonical JSON, ctd1, digest_state, and streaming array canonicalization; split into private _digest_*.py leaf modules if helpful, removing stdlib @runtime_checkable and .__dict__ usages):
    • @dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True) class Digest: scheme: str, hex: str, __str__ -> f"{self.scheme}:{self.hex}", and Digest.parse(raw: str) -> Digest splitting via scheme, sep, hex_val = raw.rsplit(":", 1) (preserving colons inside scheme names such as "sha256:file" and "h5_fixed_v1:sha256", validating 64 lowercase hex chars, and normalizing legacy "sha256:manifest-v1" if encountered).
    • Single Driver Registry (DIGEST_DRIVERS): maps scheme (sha256:file, ctd1:sha256, dir_manifest_v1:sha256, h5_fixed_v1:sha256, h5_dataset_v1:sha256, logical_matrices_canonical_v1:sha256, logical_matrices_f32_v1:sha256, output_set_v1:sha256) to one compute_digest(path, *, driver=..., member=None, options=None) -> Digest called identically by ArtifactManager, verify_artifact(), and core/admission.py.
  3. Define ArtifactResolver (from typing_extensions import Protocol, runtime_checkable) and contextvars active-resolver helpers in consist.protocols (Layer 1).
  4. Self-Contained Immutable Artifact & Plain Value Run Models (Layer 2):
  5. Artifact (@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)) stores id, key, uri, driver, digest: Digest | None, run_id, parent_artifact_id, member: str | None, facet_id: str | None, created_at: datetime, meta: Mapping[str, Any] (types.MappingProxyType over a defensive copy—truly immutable, not a dict subclass!), and _resolver_ref: weakref.ReferenceType[ArtifactResolver] | None = field(default=None, repr=False, compare=False).
  6. Provide clean .with_meta(...), .with_digest(...), .with_uri(...), and .with_resolver(...) helpers via dataclasses.replace (zero object.__setattr__!). Rewrite all in-place Artifact mutation sites (artifacts.py, tracker_archive.py, ingestion.py, artifact_schemas.py, output_sets.py, tracker.set_output_meta, workflow.py, ConsistRecord.sync_output_artifact) to replace and return updated Artifact instances in current_consist + DB (and have Tracker's PR-2 recovery_roots lookup check DB artifact.meta by art.id until PR 3 replaces recovery_roots with artifact_location).
  7. Zero hidden SQL in data fields or JSON dumps: art.uri, art.key, art.digest, art.member, art.meta, and ProvenanceWriter (consist.json) read in-memory slots directly in < 1 ms (0 SQL queries). Support round-trip serialization of Digest and MappingProxyType in ProvenanceWriter and DatabaseMaintenance.rebuild_from_json (accepting both v0.4 and v0.5 consist.json files).
  8. art.path, art.as_path(), art.ensure_local_path(), art.as_df(), and art.accessibility() delegate strictly through ArtifactResolver (_resolver_ref() or get_active_resolver()).
  9. Separate Raw File Digest from Post-dlt SQL Table State & Canonical v0.5 Run Signatures:
  10. Post-dlt global_tables ingestion never overwrites art.digest or attaches a snake-cased SQL table hash as ctd1:sha256 (B8 fix); whole-table SQL sorting/hashing during dlt append is kept out of the hot path.
  11. Freeze the canonical v0.5 input_hash (hash of sorted (role, str(artifact.digest)) pairs) and signature = sha256(f"{code_hash}:{config_hash}:{input_hash}") in PR 2 so PR 3's consist migrate and PR 4's workflow orchestration share one invariant signature definition.

items.title: Design & Implementation Blueprint
items.text:
1. Direct Upserted artifact_location Table (Cold-Archive & Overwrite Safe):
  2. Table artifact_location(location_id UUID PRIMARY KEY, digest VARCHAR, artifact_id UUID, site VARCHAR NOT NULL, mount_name VARCHAR NOT NULL, mount_instance_id VARCHAR NOT NULL, uri VARCHAR NOT NULL, member VARCHAR NOT NULL DEFAULT '', status VARCHAR NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active', witness_json JSON, observed_at_ns BIGINT NOT NULL) with indexes on (digest, status) and (artifact_id, status) plus coordinate uniqueness across (COALESCE(digest, 'id:' || CAST(artifact_id AS VARCHAR)), site, mount_name, mount_instance_id, uri, member).
  3. Workspace Instance Scoping (B7 fix): Populate mount_instance_id = sha256(str(Path(tracker.run_dir).resolve()))[:16] for "workspace" / "runs" mounts so multi-run_dir workflows sharing one provenance.duckdb never collide!
  4. Overwrite Supersession: When upserting an 'active' row at (site, mount_name, mount_instance_id, uri, member) for digest_new, mark any prior 'active' row at the same (site, mount_name, mount_instance_id, uri, member) with digest IS DISTINCT FROM digest_new as status = 'stale'.
  5. Batch location upserts at run completion (executemany), keeping 20-in/15-out warm runs fast.
  6. Racy-Safe FileStat & DirTreeStat Witnesses (src/consist/location.py, ~350 LOC):
  7. Capture (size, mtime_ns, ctime_ns, ino, racy=abs(observed_at_ns - mtime_ns) < 2_000_000_000).
  8. Proper now_ns Aging (B11 fix): FileStat.check(path, *, now_ns=None) evaluates effective_now_ns = time.time_ns() if now_ns is None else now_ns. When self.racy is True and (size, mtime_ns, ctime_ns, ino) still match: once a digest re-check passes after (effective_now_ns - st.st_mtime_ns) >= _RACY_WINDOW_NS, cache the settled FileStat(racy=False) in the in-memory location cache (and update artifact_location.witness_json if writable) so read_only=True and repeated reads never re-hash settled files!
  9. Multi-Member Container Witnesses (HDF5): When art.member is not None (e.g., /tables/households in out.h5) and another step appends a sibling member to out.h5, the enclosing file's FileStat changes while /tables/households's h5_fixed_v1:sha256 digest is unchanged. On FileStat mismatch for art.member is not None, recompute compute_digest(path, driver=art.driver, member=art.member): if it still matches art.digest, refresh witness_json to the new FileStat and return path; only mark status='stale' if the member digest changed!
  10. Shapefile Sidecar Bundle (B13 fix): Represent .shp witnesses as a DirTreeStat over all existing shapefile sidecars (.shp, .shx, .dbf, .prj, .cpg) using os.path.realpath, and stage/archive all sidecars atomically.
  11. One Verified Local-Path Resolver & Safe Scratch Eviction (B4, B6, B13 fixes):
  12. ArtifactResolver (art.path, art.as_path(), art.ensure_local_path()), consist.load(), ViewFactory, and core/admission.py all call resolve_verified_local_path(artifact, tracker=...):
    • Queries WHERE digest = ? AND status = 'active' (falling back to WHERE artifact_id = ? AND status = 'active' when artifact.digest is None on cold migrated DBs), memoized per (db_uid, location_epoch, sorted_mounts_key) (~0.03 ms warm).
    • Checks witness freshness: if FRESH, returns immediately; if scratch was overwritten, missing, or a broken symlink, verifies digest or marks 'stale' and falls through automatically to verified archive locations (staging via stage_verified_source when ensure_local_path / materialization is requested).
  13. Safe Scratch Eviction in TrackerArchiveService:
    • archive_artifact(..., mode="move") / archive_run_outputs(..., mode="move") marks the moved workspace artifact_location row status='evicted' and upserts the destination archive location as status='active'.
    • Add compact (~40 LOC) tracker.evict_artifact(artifact, *, path=None) requiring explicit witness/digest match before unlink() (never deleting user-edited scratch files!) and requiring >= 1 surviving verified 'active' archive location or ingested global_tables table.
  14. Compact, Cold-Safe consist migrate <db_path> (~350–450 LOC):
  15. Reads v0.4 DB (version=1), builds v0.5 DB in <db_path>.v05.tmp, copies global_tables.* and custom SQL views intact, verifies CHECKPOINT succeeds (never swallowing errors before .wal cleanup!), atomically backs up <db_path> to <db_path>.v04.bak, and renames <db_path>.v05.tmp -> <db_path> (plus consist migrate undo <db_path>).
  16. Deterministic v0.5 Promotion:
    1. Backfill run_artifact_link.role from run.meta["input_identity"] role bindings when present, falling back to artifact.key.
    2. Convert meta["recovery_roots"] + container_uri into artifact_location rows for every artifact (preserving artifact_id even when digest IS NULL so unmounted Lustre/NFS archives remain recoverable once mounted!).
    3. When an artifact resolves on disk under --mounts / --run-dir, compute its real v0.5 Digest + FileStat (or with --trust-v04-hashes, convert attested 64-hex v0.4 SHA-256 / manifest-v1 / logical_matrices hashes + os.stat() FileStat without re-reading multi-TB archives, while always re-hashing non-hex fast hashes).
    4. For every run whose input artifacts all have valid v0.5 Digests, recompute run.input_hash and run.signature = sha256(f"{code_hash}:{config_hash}:{input_hash}") (cacheable = True, verified by test to achieve 100% live cache-hit parity with fresh v0.5 Tracker.run); mark incomplete/cold runs cacheable = False.

items.title: Design & Implementation Blueprint
items.text:
1. Clean, Zero-Wasted-I/O Step Parameter Binding (run_invocation.py & tracker_orchestration.py):
  2. Resolve annotations per parameter (isolating closure NameErrors to that parameter instead of aborting get_type_hints() across the whole function, unwrapping typing.Annotated[T, ...] and T | None / Optional[T], and excluding reserved/injected params ctx, _consist_ctx, runtime_kwargs, and default-valued non-input params):
    • def step(x: Artifact):: always pass Artifact with zero pre-step "inputs-missing" staging/hydration I/O (B17 fix).
    • def step(x: Path): (or os.PathLike): for inputs, stage/verify local file via PR 3's resolver and pass Path (0 DataFrame load); for declared outputs={"out": path} matching parameter out: Path, inject the resolved output Path.
    • def step(x: pd.DataFrame): (or gpd.GeoDataFrame, xr.Dataset, pa.Table): load and pass the dataset via consist.load(x).
    • Unannotated def step(x):: if caller explicitly passed ExecutionOptions(input_binding="paths" | "loaded") (or legacy load_inputs=True), honor it for backward compatibility; otherwise default to passing Artifact with zero pre-step hydration I/O!
  3. Canonical outputs= (list & dict) With Directory/HDF5/Coarse-Clock Safe Staleness Guard (B9 fix):
  4. Support both outputs=["cleaned"] (return-value capture) and outputs={"cleaned": path_or_spec}.
  5. Mix declared output path specs (including full Path(p).name to preserve multi-dot stems like sim.2020.parquet and distinguish a.csv from b.csv) into config_hash only when outputs={...} declares path specs, keeping PR 2/PR 3 run signatures 100% invariant and never polluting user-visible get_run_config() with __consist_declared_outputs__.
  6. Pre-step staleness guard: before calling fn, snapshot DirTreeStat for directories/Zarr stores (not top-level os.stat(dir)), pre-step member digest for multi-member HDF5 outputs (OutputArtifactSpec(..., member=...)), or FileStat (+ lazy pre-step digest fallback) for regular files. If a pre-existing target has identical post-step stat AND identical content/member digest (handling coarse filesystem clock ticks where deterministic rewrites keep size/mtime unchanged vs genuinely untouched stale files), raise StaleOutputError(RuntimeError) instead of logging untouched stale disk bytes!
  7. Sub-Millisecond Ephemeral Mode (Tracker()) vs JSON-Only Mode vs Ghost Mode (B11 fix):
  8. Default run_dir: Path | str | None = None on Tracker.__init__ and FileSystemManager.__init__.
  9. Ephemeral Mode (db_path=None, run_dir=None): no mkdir, no DatabaseManager, no ProvenanceWriter / consist.json, lightweight FileStat only (~0.1 ms execution even on 50 MB files, replacing all 818 LOC of NoopTracker).
  10. JSON-Only Mode (db_path=None, run_dir=<path>): preserves full Digest computation and consist.json writing for DB-less HPC workers reconstructed via rebuild_from_json().
  11. Preserve "Ghost Mode" terminology in docs strictly for its established Consist meaning (provenance + hot global_tables retained after cold/scratch files are evicted).
  12. Lazy, Verified Coupler (B10 fix):

items.title: Goal
items.text: Extend Consist's experimental static LinkML release into a portable provenance graph. provenance.yaml supplies durable lineage facts; binding.yaml adds cache-aware invocation facts. LinkML remains a development-only dependency. The schema stays experimental version 0.1.0, independently versioned from the Python package.

items.title: Module boundary
items.text:
provenance.yaml defines ConsistProvenanceContext (required stable namespace and optional mutable locator), ConsistRunReference (optional model name, parent run, and config/input/git identity evidence), ConsistArtifactReference (portable fingerprint, trusted immutable identity, optional parent artifact, optional producing run), ConsistArtifactIdentity, ConsistRunArtifactAssociation, and ConsistProvenanceDocument (an enclosing context plus graph facts).

ConsistArtifactIdentity is constrained to what Consist can currently attest: algorithm sha256, kind file or manifest-v1, and a lowercase 64-character SHA-256 digest. fingerprint remains the broader public Artifact.hash, which may be content- or metadata-based; database-local Artifact.content_id is excluded.

ConsistRunArtifactAssociation requires run, artifact, and input/output direction. Its role, binding parameter, and implicitness are optional evidence because the persisted RunArtifactLink only guarantees direction and implicitness. A role is invocation-specific and never substitutes for an artifact key.

binding.yaml imports provenance.yaml and defines ConsistBindingInvocationReference: requested run, effective execution run, optional cache-source run, required cache outcome, and optional strict binding identity digest. It excludes opaque binding JSON.

items.title: Identity and context rules
items.text:
The identity of a run or artifact is (namespace, local ID). A record's provenance_context overrides the enclosing ConsistProvenanceDocument.provenance_context; when the record omits it, it inherits that enclosing context. A standalone record without either context is local to its containing handoff and cannot be safely merged with another document. The locator is mutable retrieval metadata only, never part of identity, equality, deduplication, or namespace assignment.

The same run_id or artifact_id in two namespaces is distinct. A cross-reference is consistent only when its resolved (namespace, local ID) matches its target record.

items.title: Production and consumption graph rules
items.text:
For an output association, if the artifact supplies producing_run, it MUST resolve to the association's run after context inheritance. An output association with no producing_run is still a production assertion; consumers MUST NOT add a contradictory producing run. A producing run and matching output association state the same production fact twice for convenient traversal, not two events.

An input association means the run consumed or used the artifact; it makes no production claim. An absent producing run is valid for an external input. Parent artifact records container/member structure only and is not a derivation edge.

items.title: Cache-aware invocation rules
items.text:
requested_run is the current invocation's run. effective_execution_run supplied the result. cache_source_run is present only for a cache hit that reused a historical producer. cache_outcome is exactly miss or hit.

Cache outcome requested run effective execution run cache-source run miss newly executing run same newly executing run omitted hit current invocation's new run historical producer same historical producer

For a miss, requested and effective runs MUST resolve to the same run and cache source MUST be absent. For a hit, effective and cache-source runs MUST resolve to the same historical producer, which MUST NOT be overwritten with the current requested invocation's input intent. The optional binding identity digest is the lowercase SHA-256 digest of a strict resolved-binding identity; it identifies the binding contract, not an artifact or opaque evidence document.

items.title: Deliberate exclusions and verification
items.text:
The release excludes mutable locations and recovery paths; status, timestamps, descriptions, tags, arbitrary metadata, and scenario fields; schema profiles, observations, manifests, admission reports, registry aliases, full resolved-binding JSON, and PILATES-owned scenario semantics.

The release builder publishes modular and merged assets for both modules, generated reference documentation, and checksums. Downstreams pin checked immutable merged assets rather than resolve remote imports. Tests cover module linting and composition; production and consumption lineage; cache hit and miss; file and manifest-v1 identities; nested runs; parent artifacts; identical local IDs under distinct namespaces; both merged assets and checksums; and the zero-LinkML-runtime-import boundary.
